    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

Test Implementation:
func TestCollectRaw_Success_123(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    scraper := &Scraper{
        address:         "http://example.com",
        simpleMetrics:   []string{"metric1", "metric2"},
        histogramMetrics: []string{"histogram1"},
    }

    mockStats := map[string]interface{}{
        "metric1": 1.0,
        "metric2": 2.0,
        "histogram1.count": 10.0,
        "histogram1.sum": 100.0,
        "histogram1.count_per_bucket": []interface{}{1.0, 2.0, 3.0},
        "histogram1.bounds": []interface{}{10.0, 20.0},
    }

    httpGet = func(url string) (*http.Response, error) {
        if url == scraper.address {
            body := `{
                "metric1": 1.0,
                "metric2": 2.0,
                "histogram1.count": 10.0,
                "histogram1.sum": 100.0,
                "histogram1.count_per_bucket": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0],
                "histogram1.bounds": [10.0, 20.0]
            }`
            return &http.Response{
                StatusCode: http.StatusOK,
                Body:       io.NopCloser(strings.NewReader(body)),
            }, nil
        }
        return nil, errors.New("unexpected URL")
    }

    // Act
    metrics, err := scraper.CollectRaw()

    // Assert
    require.NoError(t, err)
    require.NotNil(t, metrics)
    assert.Equal(t, 1.0, metrics["metric1"])
    assert.Equal(t, 2.0, metrics["metric2"])
    assert.Equal(t, 1.0, metrics["up"])
    histogram, ok := metrics["histogram1"].(*histogram)
    require.True(t, ok)
    assert.Equal(t, uint64(10), histogram.count)
    assert.Equal(t, 100.0, histogram.sum)
    assert.Equal(t, map[float64]uint64{10.0: 1, 20.0: 3}, histogram.buckets)
}

func TestCollectRaw_Success_001(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    scraper := &Scraper{
        address:         "http://example.com",
        simpleMetrics:   []string{"metric1", "metric2"},
        histogramMetrics: []string{"histogram1"},
    }

    mockResponse := `{
        "metric1": 1.0,
        "metric2": 2.0,
        "histogram1.count": 10.0,
        "histogram1.sum": 100.0,
        "histogram1.count_per_bucket": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0],
        "histogram1.bounds": [10.0, 20.0]
    }`

    httpClient := &http.Client{}
    httpGetMock := func(url string) (*http.Response, error) {
        if url == scraper.address {
            return &http.Response{
                StatusCode: http.StatusOK,
                Body:       io.NopCloser(strings.NewReader(mockResponse)),
            }, nil
        }
        return nil, errors.New("unexpected URL")
    }

    // Mock http.Get
    originalHTTPGet := httpGet
    defer func() { httpGet = originalHTTPGet }()
    httpGet = httpGetMock

    // Act
    metrics, err := scraper.CollectRaw()

    // Assert
    require.NoError(t, err)
    require.NotNil(t, metrics)
    assert.Equal(t, 1.0, metrics["metric1"])
    assert.Equal(t, 2.0, metrics["metric2"])
    assert.Equal(t, 1.0, metrics["up"])
    histogram, ok := metrics["histogram1"].(*histogram)
    require.True(t, ok)
    assert.Equal(t, uint64(10), histogram.count)
    assert.Equal(t, 100.0, histogram.sum)
    assert.Equal(t, map[float64]uint64{10.0: 1, 20.0: 3}, histogram.buckets)
}

func TestValidatorInit_ValidConfig_123(t *testing.T) {
    validConfig := `{
        "host_url": "https://example.com",
        "languages": ["en", "es"],
        "universal_templ": "{{.Code}} is your verification code for {{.HostUrl}}",
        "sender": "TestSender",
        "debug_response": "123456",
        "max_retries": 5,
        "code_length": 6,
        "twilio_conf": {}
    }`

    mockValidate := new(validateMocks.Validator)
    mockValidate.On("ValidateHostURL", "https://example.com").Return("https://example.com", nil)
    mockValidate.On("ReadTemplateFile", mock.Anything, "en").Return(&textt.Template{}, "", nil)
    mockValidate.On("ReadTemplateFile", mock.Anything, "es").Return(&textt.Template{}, "", nil)

    v := &validator{}
    err := v.Init(validConfig)

    require.NoError(t, err)
    assert.Equal(t, "https://example.com", v.HostUrl)
    assert.Equal(t, []string{"en", "es"}, v.Languages)
    assert.Equal(t, "TestSender", v.Sender)
    assert.Equal(t, "123456", v.DebugResponse)
    assert.Equal(t, 5, v.MaxRetries)
    assert.Equal(t, 6, v.CodeLength)
    assert.NotNil(t, v.universalTempl)
    assert.NotNil(t, v.langMatcher)
    assert.NotNil(t, v.maxCodeValue)

    mockValidate.AssertExpectations(t)
}

Test Implementation:
func TestDecodeGoogleApiError_UnrecognizedDetailsFormat_013(t *testing.T) {
    googleErr := &googleapi.Error{
        Code:    400,
        Message: "Bad Request",
        Errors: []googleapi.ErrorItem{
            {Reason: "invalidArgument", Message: "Invalid argument provided"},
        },
        Details: []interface{}{
            map[string]interface{}{
                "@type": "unknown.type",
            },
        },
    }
    decoded, errs := DecodeGoogleApiError(googleErr)
    assert.Equal(t, 400, decoded.HttpCode)
    assert.Contains(t, decoded.ErrMessage, "Bad Request")
    assert.Contains(t, decoded.ErrMessage, "invalidArgument/Invalid argument provided")
    assert.Equal(t, string(ErrorUnspecified), decoded.FcmErrCode)
    assert.Len(t, errs, 1)
    assert.Contains(t, errs[0].Error(), "error.Details unrecognized format")
}

import (
    "testing"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
    "text/template"
)

Required Library Installation
go get github.com/stretchr/testify

Test Implementation:
func TestExecuteTemplate_ValidAndInvalidInputs_002(t *testing.T) {
    tmpl := template.Must(template.New("test").Parse("Hello, {{.Name}}!"))
    parts := []string{"test"}
    params := map[string]interface{}{"Name": "World"}

    t.Run("Valid Template Execution", func(t *testing.T) {
        result, err := ExecuteTemplate(tmpl, parts, params)
        require.NoError(t, err)
        assert.Equal(t, "Hello, World!", result["test"])
    })

    t.Run("Invalid Template Execution", func(t *testing.T) {
        tmplInvalid := template.Must(template.New("test").Parse("Hello, {{.InvalidKey}}!"))
        _, err := ExecuteTemplate(tmplInvalid, parts, params)
        require.Error(t, err)
    })

    t.Run("Nil Parts", func(t *testing.T) {
        result, err := ExecuteTemplate(tmpl, nil, params)
        require.NoError(t, err)
        assert.Equal(t, "Hello, World!", result[""])
    })
}

Test Implementation:
func TestPayloadToData_ValidPayload_123(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    timestamp := time.Now()
    payload := &push.Payload{
        What:        push.ActMsg,
        Silent:      true,
        Topic:       "test_topic",
        Timestamp:   timestamp,
        From:        "usr123",
        SeqId:       42,
        ContentType: "text/plain",
        Content:     "Hello, World!",
        Webrtc:      "started",
        AudioOnly:   true,
        Replace:     "seq123",
    }

    // Mock drafty.PlainText and drafty.Preview
    mockDrafty := new(draftyMocks.Drafty)
    mockDrafty.On("PlainText", payload.Content).Return("Hello, World!", nil)
    mockDrafty.On("Preview", payload.Content, push.MaxPayloadLength).Return("Hello, World!", nil)

    // Act
    data, err := payloadToData(payload)

    // Assert
    require.NoError(t, err)
    require.NotNil(t, data)
    assert.Equal(t, "msg", data["what"])
    assert.Equal(t, "true", data["silent"])
    assert.Equal(t, "test_topic", data["topic"])
    assert.Equal(t, timestamp.Format(time.RFC3339Nano), data["ts"])
    assert.Equal(t, "usr123", data["xfrom"])
    assert.Equal(t, "42", data["seq"])
    assert.Equal(t, "text/plain", data["mime"])
    assert.Equal(t, "Hello, World!", data["content"])
    assert.Equal(t, "Hello, World!", data["rc"])
    assert.Equal(t, "started", data["webrtc"])
    assert.Equal(t, "true", data["aonly"])
    assert.Equal(t, "true", data["silent"])
    assert.Equal(t, "seq123", data["replace"])

    // Verify mocks
    mockDrafty.AssertExpectations(t)
}

func TestExecuteTemplate_ValidAndInvalidInputs_002(t *testing.T) {
    tmpl := template.Must(template.New("test").Parse("Hello, {{.Name}}!"))
    parts := []string{"test"}
    params := map[string]interface{}{"Name": "World"}

    t.Run("Valid Template Execution", func(t *testing.T) {
        result, err := ExecuteTemplate(tmpl, parts, params)
        require.NoError(t, err)
        assert.Equal(t, "Hello, World!", result["test"])
    })

    t.Run("Invalid Template Execution", func(t *testing.T) {
        tmplInvalid := template.Must(template.New("test").Parse("Hello, {{.InvalidKey}}!"))
        _, err := ExecuteTemplate(tmplInvalid, parts, params)
        require.Error(t, err)
    })

    t.Run("Nil Parts", func(t *testing.T) {
        result, err := ExecuteTemplate(tmpl, nil, params)
        require.NoError(t, err)
        assert.Equal(t, "Hello, World!", result[""])
    })
}

func TestCollectRaw_Success_281(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
        // Note: Using float64 for numbers as expected by json.Unmarshal into interface{}
        fmt.Fprintln(w, `{
            "simple": 10.0,
            "histo.count": 5.0,

            "histo.count_per_bucket": [1.0, 4.0],
            "histo.bounds": [10.0]
        }`)
    }))
    defer server.Close()

    scraper := &Scraper{

        simpleMetrics:   []string{"simple"},
        histogramMetrics: []string{"histo"},

    // Assert
    require.NoError(t, err)

    require.True(t, ok, "histo metric should be a *histogram")

func TestNewInfluxDBExporter_Version2_0_123(t *testing.T) {
    scraper := &Scraper{} // Using the actual struct as it's not an interface
    influxDBVersion := "2.0"
    pushBaseAddress := "http://localhost:8086"
    organization := "test-org"
    bucket := "test-bucket"
    token := "test-token"
    instance := "test-instance"

    exporter := NewInfluxDBExporter(influxDBVersion, pushBaseAddress, organization, bucket, token, instance, scraper)

    require.NotNil(t, exporter)
    // Expected URL format for v2.0
    expectedTargetAddress := "http://localhost:8086/api/v2/write?bucket=test-bucket&org=test-org"
    parsedExpected, _ := url.Parse(expectedTargetAddress)
    parsedActual, _ := url.Parse(exporter.targetAddress)

    // Compare URLs ignoring query parameter order
    assert.Equal(t, parsedExpected.Scheme, parsedActual.Scheme)
    assert.Equal(t, parsedExpected.Host, parsedActual.Host)
    assert.Equal(t, parsedExpected.Path, parsedActual.Path)
    assert.Equal(t, parsedExpected.Query(), parsedActual.Query())


    // Expected header format for v2.0
    assert.Equal(t, "Token test-token", exporter.tokenHeader)
    assert.Equal(t, organization, exporter.organization)
    assert.Equal(t, bucket, exporter.bucket)
    assert.Equal(t, instance, exporter.instance)
    assert.Same(t, scraper, exporter.scraper) // Check if it's the same instance
}

import (
	"fmt"
	"io/ioutil"
	"net/http"
	"strconv"
	"strings"

	"time"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/mock"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

Test Implementation:
func TestPush_Success_242(t *testing.T) {
    // --- Arrange ---
    mockScraper := &mockScraper{}
    metrics := map[string]interface{}{
        "live_connections": float64(150.0),
        "request_latency": &histogram{
            count:   100,
            sum:     550.5,
            buckets: map[float64]uint64{0.1: 20, 0.5: 50, 1.0: 30},
        },
    }
    mockScraper.On("CollectRaw").Return(metrics, nil)

    exporter := &InfluxDBExporter{
        targetAddress: "http://fake-influx:8086/api/v2/write?bucket=b&org=o",
        tokenHeader:   "Token fake-token",
        instance:      "test-instance-1",
        scraper:       mockScraper, // Use the mock scraper
    }

    // Mock HTTP client
    mockRT := &mockRoundTripper{}
    mockRT.RoundTripFunc = func(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
        // Assert request details
        assert.Equal(t, "POST", req.Method)
        assert.Equal(t, exporter.targetAddress, req.URL.String())
        assert.Equal(t, exporter.tokenHeader, req.Header.Get("Authorization"))

        bodyBytes, err := ioutil.ReadAll(req.Body)
        require.NoError(t, err)
        bodyString := string(bodyBytes)

        // Check if metrics are present (order independent)
        assert.Contains(t, bodyString, "live_connections,instance=test-instance-1 value=150.000000 ")
        assert.Contains(t, bodyString, "request_latency,instance=test-instance-1 count=100 ")
        assert.Contains(t, bodyString, "request_latency,instance=test-instance-1 sum=550.500000 ")
        assert.Contains(t, bodyString, "request_latency,instance=test-instance-1 le=0.100000,value=20 ")
        assert.Contains(t, bodyString, "request_latency,instance=test-instance-1 le=0.500000,value=50 ")
        assert.Contains(t, bodyString, "request_latency,instance=test-instance-1 le=1.000000,value=30 ")

        // Check timestamps (allow small variation, check only one line)
        lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(bodyString), "\n")
        require.NotEmpty(t, lines)
        parts := strings.Fields(lines[0])
        require.True(t, len(parts) >= 3)
        ts, err := strconv.ParseInt(parts[len(parts)-1], 10, 64)
        require.NoError(t, err)
        assert.InDelta(t, time.Now().UnixNano(), ts, float64(5*time.Second)) // Allow 5 sec diff

        // Return success response
        return &http.Response{
            StatusCode: http.StatusOK, // 200 OK
            Body:       ioutil.NopCloser(strings.NewReader("")),
            Header:     make(http.Header),
        }, nil
    }
    originalClient := http.DefaultClient
    http.DefaultClient = &http.Client{Transport: mockRT}
    defer func() { http.DefaultClient = originalClient }() // Restore original client

    // --- Act ---
    err := exporter.Push()

    // --- Assert ---
    assert.NoError(t, err)
    mockScraper.AssertExpectations(t)
    // mockRT doesn't use testify/mock, assertion is done within RoundTripFunc
}

Test Implementation:
func TestPush_HTTPClientDoError_464(t *testing.T) {
    // --- Arrange ---
    mockScraper := &mockScraper{}
    metrics := map[string]interface{}{"metric": float64(1.0)}
    mockScraper.On("CollectRaw").Return(metrics, nil)

    exporter := &InfluxDBExporter{
        targetAddress: "http://fake-influx:8086/api/v2/write?bucket=b&org=o",
        tokenHeader:   "Token fake-token",
        instance:      "test-instance-2",
        scraper:       mockScraper,
    }

    // Mock HTTP client to return an error
    mockRT := &mockRoundTripper{}
    expectedError := fmt.Errorf("network connection refused")
    mockRT.RoundTripFunc = func(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
        return nil, expectedError
    }
    originalClient := http.DefaultClient
    http.DefaultClient = &http.Client{Transport: mockRT}
    defer func() { http.DefaultClient = originalClient }()

    // --- Act ---
    err := exporter.Push()

    // --- Assert ---
    require.Error(t, err)
    assert.Equal(t, expectedError, err) // Check for the exact error instance
    mockScraper.AssertExpectations(t)
}

Test Implementation:
func TestPush_HTTPResponseError_575(t *testing.T) {
    // --- Arrange ---
    mockScraper := &mockScraper{}
    metrics := map[string]interface{}{"metric": float64(2.0)}
    mockScraper.On("CollectRaw").Return(metrics, nil)

    exporter := &InfluxDBExporter{
        targetAddress: "http://fake-influx:8086/api/v2/write?bucket=b&org=o",
        tokenHeader:   "Token fake-token",
        instance:      "test-instance-3",
        scraper:       mockScraper,
    }

    // Mock HTTP client to return a 400 Bad Request
    mockRT := &mockRoundTripper{}
    responseBody := `{"code":"invalid","message":"unable to parse points"}`
    mockRT.RoundTripFunc = func(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
        return &http.Response{
            StatusCode: http.StatusBadRequest, // 400
            Status:     "400 Bad Request",
            Body:       ioutil.NopCloser(strings.NewReader(responseBody)),
            Header:     make(http.Header),
        }, nil
    }
    originalClient := http.DefaultClient
    http.DefaultClient = &http.Client{Transport: mockRT}
    defer func() { http.DefaultClient = originalClient }()

    // --- Act ---
    err := exporter.Push()

    // --- Assert ---
    require.Error(t, err)
    expectedErrorMsg := fmt.Sprintf("HTTP %s: %s", "400 Bad Request", responseBody)
    assert.Equal(t, expectedErrorMsg, err.Error())
    mockScraper.AssertExpectations(t)
}

Test Implementation:
func TestPush_HTTPResponseError_BodyReadError_686(t *testing.T) {
    // --- Arrange ---
    mockScraper := &mockScraper{}
    metrics := map[string]interface{}{"metric": float64(3.0)}
    mockScraper.On("CollectRaw").Return(metrics, nil)

    exporter := &InfluxDBExporter{
        targetAddress: "http://fake-influx:8086/api/v2/write?bucket=b&org=o",
        tokenHeader:   "Token fake-token",
        instance:      "test-instance-4",
        scraper:       mockScraper,
    }

    // Mock HTTP client with a faulty response body reader
    mockRT := &mockRoundTripper{}
    readError := fmt.Errorf("failed to read response body")
    mockBody := &mockReadCloser{ReadErr: readError} // Custom mock reader

    mockRT.RoundTripFunc = func(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
        return &http.Response{
            StatusCode: http.StatusInternalServerError, // 500
            Status:     "500 Internal Server Error",
            Body:       mockBody, // Use the mock reader that will fail
            Header:     make(http.Header),
        }, nil
    }
    originalClient := http.DefaultClient
    http.DefaultClient = &http.Client{Transport: mockRT}
    defer func() { http.DefaultClient = originalClient }()

    // --- Act ---
    err := exporter.Push()

    // --- Assert ---
    require.Error(t, err)
    // The error message should contain the status and the body read error
    expectedErrorMsg := fmt.Sprintf("HTTP %s: %s", "500 Internal Server Error", readError.Error())
    assert.Equal(t, expectedErrorMsg, err.Error())
    mockScraper.AssertExpectations(t)
}

func TestDecodeGoogleApiError_GoogleApiError_InvalidErrorCodeType_112(t *testing.T) {
	// Case 1: errorCode is not a string
	googleErr1 := &googleapi.Error{
		Code:    400,
		Message: "Bad Request",
		Details: []interface{}{
			map[string]interface{}{
				"@type":     "type.googleapis.com/google.firebase.fcm.v1.FcmError",
				"errorCode": 12345, // Not a string
			},
		},
	}
	decoded1, errs1 := DecodeGoogleApiError(googleErr1)
	assert.Equal(t, 400, decoded1.HttpCode)
	assert.Equal(t, ErrorUnspecified, decoded1.FcmErrCode) // Default because errorCode is wrong type
	assert.Empty(t, errs1)

	// Case 2: errorCode field is missing
	googleErr2 := &googleapi.Error{
		Code:    400,
		Message: "Bad Request",
		Details: []interface{}{
			map[string]interface{}{
				"@type": "type.googleapis.com/google.firebase.fcm.v1.FcmError",
				// "errorCode" field is missing
			},
		},
	}
	decoded2, errs2 := DecodeGoogleApiError(googleErr2)
	assert.Equal(t, 400, decoded2.HttpCode)
	assert.Equal(t, ErrorUnspecified, decoded2.FcmErrCode) // Default because errorCode is missing
	assert.Empty(t, errs2)
}

func TestReadTemplateFile_PathExecuteError_181(t *testing.T) {
  // Path template expects {{.Lang}}, but we provide {{.Language}}
  pathTempl, err := template.New("path").Parse("{{.Lang}}/file.tmpl") // Mismatched key
  require.NoError(t, err)
  lang := "en" // This won't match ".Lang"

  require.Error(t, err)

  assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "map has no entry for key \"Lang\"")
  assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "reading") // Check for the wrapping error message

import (
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"testing"
	"text/template"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

Required Library Installation
# No new libraries needed

Test Implementation:
func TestReadTemplateFile_ParseFileError_BadSyntax_201(t *testing.T) {
  tempDir := t.TempDir()
  lang := "fr"
  templateFileName := "bad_syntax.tmpl"
  // Invalid template content
  templateContent := "Hello {{ .Name" // Missing closing braces

  // Path template generates path like: /tmp/somedir/fr/bad_syntax.tmpl
  pathTempl, err := template.New("path").Parse(filepath.Join(tempDir, "{{.Language}}", templateFileName))
  require.NoError(t, err)

  // Create the directory and the invalid template file
  langDir := filepath.Join(tempDir, lang)
  err = os.MkdirAll(langDir, 0755)
  require.NoError(t, err)
  templateFilePath := filepath.Join(langDir, templateFileName)
  err = os.WriteFile(templateFilePath, []byte(templateContent), 0644)
  require.NoError(t, err)

  // Execute the function under test
  _, resolvedPath, err := ReadTemplateFile(pathTempl, lang)

  // Assertions
  require.Error(t, err) // Expect a template parsing error
  assert.Equal(t, templateFilePath, resolvedPath)
  assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "template: bad_syntax.tmpl:") // Error should mention the file and location
  assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "unexpected")                  // Specific template parsing error message part
}

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

Test Implementation:
func TestParseHisto_Success_734(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    stats := map[string]interface{}{
        "histo.count":             10.0,
        "histo.sum":               100.0,
        "histo.count_per_bucket": []interface{}{1.0, 2.0, 7.0}, // Cumulative: 1, 3, 10
        "histo.bounds":           []interface{}{10.0, 20.0},
    }
    key := "histo"
    expectedBuckets := map[float64]uint64{
        10.0: 1, // buckets[0]
        20.0: 3, // buckets[0] + buckets[1]
        // The last bucket count (7.0) corresponds to +Inf and isn't directly in the map keys
    }

    // Act
    h, err := parseHisto(stats, key)

    // Assert
    require.NoError(t, err)
    require.NotNil(t, h)
    assert.Equal(t, uint64(10), h.count)
    assert.Equal(t, 100.0, h.sum)
    assert.Equal(t, expectedBuckets, h.buckets)
}

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

Test Implementation:
func TestParseStatsRaw_Success_717(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    scraper := &Scraper{
        simpleMetrics:    []string{"simple1", "simple2.nested"},
        histogramMetrics: []string{"histo1"},
    }
    stats := map[string]interface{}{
        "simple1": 1.0,
        "simple2": map[string]interface{}{
            "nested": 2.0,
        },
        "histo1.count":             5.0,
        "histo1.sum":               50.0,
        "histo1.count_per_bucket": []interface{}{1.0, 4.0}, // Cumulative: 1, 5
        "histo1.bounds":           []interface{}{10.0},
    }
    expectedHistoBuckets := map[float64]uint64{
        10.0: 1, // buckets[0]
    }

    // Act
    metrics, err := scraper.parseStatsRaw(stats)

    // Assert
    require.NoError(t, err)
    require.NotNil(t, metrics)
    assert.Len(t, metrics, 3) // simple1, simple2.nested, histo1
    assert.Equal(t, 1.0, metrics["simple1"])
    assert.Equal(t, 2.0, metrics["simple2.nested"])

    histo, ok := metrics["histo1"].(*histogram)
    require.True(t, ok, "histo1 metric should be of type *histogram")
    assert.Equal(t, uint64(5), histo.count)
    assert.Equal(t, 50.0, histo.sum)
    assert.Equal(t, expectedHistoBuckets, histo.buckets)
}

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

Test Implementation:
func TestCollectRaw_Success_281(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
        // Note: Using float64 for numbers as expected by json.Unmarshal into interface{}
        fmt.Fprintln(w, `{
            "simple": 10.0,
            "histo.count": 5.0,
            "histo.sum": 50.0,
            "histo.count_per_bucket": [1.0, 4.0],
            "histo.bounds": [10.0]
        }`)
    }))
    defer server.Close()

    scraper := &Scraper{
        address:         server.URL,
        simpleMetrics:   []string{"simple"},
        histogramMetrics: []string{"histo"},
    }
    expectedHistoBuckets := map[float64]uint64{
        10.0: 1, // buckets[0]
    }

    // Act
    metrics, err := scraper.CollectRaw()

    // Assert
    require.NoError(t, err)
    require.NotNil(t, metrics)
    require.Len(t, metrics, 3) // simple, histo, up

    // Check 'up' metric
    upMetric, ok := metrics["up"]
    require.True(t, ok, "'up' metric should exist")
    assert.Equal(t, 1.0, upMetric, "'up' metric should be 1.0")

    // Check 'simple' metric
    simpleMetric, ok := metrics["simple"]
    require.True(t, ok, "'simple' metric should exist")
    assert.Equal(t, 10.0, simpleMetric)

    // Check 'histo' metric
    histoMetric, ok := metrics["histo"]
    require.True(t, ok, "'histo' metric should exist")
    histo, ok := histoMetric.(*histogram)
    require.True(t, ok, "'histo' metric should be a *histogram")
    assert.Equal(t, uint64(5), histo.count)
    assert.Equal(t, 50.0, histo.sum)
    assert.Equal(t, expectedHistoBuckets, histo.buckets)
}

                Password: "(random)",
                State:    "ok",
            },
        },
        datapath: ".",
    }
    expectedUserID := "usrRandPass1"
    expectedUserUID := types.ParseUserId(expectedUserID)

    mockAuthHandler.On("Init", mock.Anything, mock.Anything).Return(nil).Once() // Init call

        args.Get(0).(*types.User).Id = expectedUserID
        args.Get(0).(*types.User).ObjHeader.SetUid(expectedUserUID)
    }).Return(expectedUserID, nil).Once()

    // Expect AddRecord to be called with a generated password (length 8)
    mockAuthHandler.On("AddRecord", mock.MatchedBy(func(rec *auth.Rec) bool {
        return rec.Uid == expectedUserUID && rec.AuthLevel == auth.LevelAuth
    }), mock.MatchedBy(func(secret []byte) bool {

        return len(parts) == 2 && parts[0] == "botuser" && len(parts[1]) == 8
    }), "").Return("auth-rec-id", nil).Once()

    // Act
    genDb(inputData)

    // Assert
    mockAuthHandler.AssertExpectations(t)
    mockUsers.AssertExpectations(t)
    mockSubs.AssertExpectations(t)

    // Cleanup
    store.Store = nil
    delete(auth.Available, "basic")

    mockUsers := new(storeMocks.Users)
    mockTopics := new(storeMocks.Topics)
    mockSubs := new(storeMocks.Subs) // Subs mock needed for user creation if any

    store.Store.SetAdapter(mockUsers, mockSubs, mockTopics, nil, nil) // Set Topics adapter

        return mockAuthHandler, nil
    })

    ownerUserID := "usrOwner123"
    ownerUID := types.ParseUserId(ownerUserID)

    inputData := &Data{
        Users: []User{ // Need at least one user to be the owner
            {Username: "owner", Password: "pw", State: "ok"},
        },
        Grouptopics: []GroupTopic{
            {
                Name:         "coolgroup",
                Owner:        "owner", // Refers to the user above
                Channel:      false,
                Access:       DefAccess{Auth: "RWPSA", Anon: "R"},
                Tags:         []string{"group", "test"},
                Public:       theCard{Fn: "Cool Group"},
                Trusted:      tTrusted{Val: "trusted-info"},
                CreatedAt:    "-2h",
                OwnerPrivate: tPrivate{Comment: "owner stuff"},
            },
        },
        datapath: ".",
    }

    // Mock user creation part
    mockAuthHandler.On("Init", mock.Anything, mock.Anything).Return(nil).Once()
    mockUsers.On("Create", mock.AnythingOfType("*types.User"), mock.Anything).Run(func(args mock.Arguments) {
        args.Get(0).(*types.User).Id = ownerUserID
        args.Get(0).(*types.User).ObjHeader.SetUid(ownerUID)
    }).Return(ownerUserID, nil).Once()
    mockAuthHandler.On("AddRecord", mock.Anything, mock.Anything, mock.Anything).Return("auth-rec-id", nil).Once()


    // Mock topic creation part
    expectedAuthMode := types.ModeCRWPSA
    expectedAnonMode := types.ModeCReadOnly
    expectedOwnerPrivate := map[string]interface{}{"comment": "owner stuff"} // Convert tPrivate

    mockTopics.On("Create", mock.MatchedBy(func(topic *types.Topic) bool {
        isOk := topic.Id != "" && // genTopicName generates something
            topic.Owner == ownerUID.String() &&
            topic.Access.Auth == expectedAuthMode &&
            topic.Access.Anon == expectedAnonMode &&
            !topic.UseBt && // Channel is false
            assert.ObjectsAreEqual(map[string]string{"val": "trusted-info"}, topic.Trusted) &&
            assert.ObjectsAreEqual([]string{"group", "test"}, topic.Tags) &&
            assert.NotNil(t, topic.Public) && topic.Public.(*card).Fn == "Cool Group" &&
            assert.True(t, topic.Acs.GetAccess(ownerUID).IsOwner()) // Check owner access
        topic.ObjHeader.SetUid(types.ParseUid(topic.Id)) // Ensure Uid is set for logging/index
        return isOk
    }), ownerUID, expectedOwnerPrivate).Return(nil).Once()


    // Act
    genDb(inputData)

    // Assert
    mockAuthHandler.AssertExpectations(t)
    mockUsers.AssertExpectations(t)
    mockTopics.AssertExpectations(t)
    mockSubs.AssertExpectations(t)

    // Cleanup
    store.Store = nil
    delete(auth.Available, "basic")
}

    // Arrange
    mockAuthHandler := new(authMocks.AuthHandler)
    mockUsers := new(storeMocks.Users)
    mockTopics := new(storeMocks.Topics)
    mockSubs := new(storeMocks.Subs)
    store.Store = &store.Plex{}
    store.Store.SetAdapter(mockUsers, mockSubs, mockTopics, nil, nil)
    store.RegisterAuthScheme("basic", func(_ []byte) (auth.AuthHandler, error) {
        return mockAuthHandler, nil
    })

    user1ID := "usrUserP2P1"
    user1UID := types.ParseUserId(user1ID)
    user2ID := "usrUserP2P2"
    user2UID := types.ParseUserId(user2ID)

    inputData := &Data{
        Users: []User{ // Need users for P2P
            {Username: "user1", Password: "pw1", State: "ok"},
            {Username: "user2", Password: "pw2", State: "ok"},
        },
        P2psubs: []P2PSub{
            {
                Users: []P2PUser{
                    {Name: "user1", Want: "RW", Have: "R", Private: tPrivate{Comment: "u1 priv"}},
                    {Name: "user2"}, // Default P2P modes
                },
                CreatedAt: "-3h",
            },
        },
        datapath: ".",
    }

    // Mock user creation
    mockAuthHandler.On("Init", mock.Anything, mock.Anything).Return(nil).Once()
    mockUsers.On("Create", mock.MatchedBy(func(u *types.User) bool { return u.Tags[0] == "basic:user1" }), mock.Anything).Run(func(args mock.Arguments) { args.Get(0).(*types.User).Id = user1ID; args.Get(0).(*types.User).ObjHeader.SetUid(user1UID) }).Return(user1ID, nil).Once()
    mockUsers.On("Create", mock.MatchedBy(func(u *types.User) bool { return u.Tags[0] == "basic:user2" }), mock.Anything).Run(func(args mock.Arguments) { args.Get(0).(*types.User).Id = user2ID; args.Get(0).(*types.User).ObjHeader.SetUid(user2UID) }).Return(user2ID, nil).Once()
    mockAuthHandler.On("AddRecord", mock.Anything, mock.Anything, mock.Anything).Return("auth-rec-id", nil).Twice()


    // Mock P2P creation
    expectedTopicName := user1UID.P2PName(user2UID)
    expectedPrivate1 := map[string]interface{}{"comment": "u1 priv"}

    mockTopics.On("CreateP2P",
        mock.MatchedBy(func(sub1 *types.Subscription) bool {
            return sub1.User == user1ID && sub1.Topic == expectedTopicName &&
                sub1.ModeWant == types.ModeCRW && sub1.ModeGiven == types.ModeCReadOnly &&
                assert.ObjectsAreEqual(expectedPrivate1, sub1.Private)
        }),
        mock.MatchedBy(func(sub2 *types.Subscription) bool {
            return sub2.User == user2ID && sub2.Topic == expectedTopicName &&
                sub2.ModeWant == types.ModeCP2P && sub2.ModeGiven == types.ModeCP2P && // Defaults
                assert.Nil(t, sub2.Private)
        })).Return(nil).Once()

    // Act
    genDb(inputData)

    // Assert
    mockAuthHandler.AssertExpectations(t)
    mockUsers.AssertExpectations(t)
    mockTopics.AssertExpectations(t)
    mockSubs.AssertExpectations(t)

    // Cleanup
    store.Store = nil
    delete(auth.Available, "basic")
}

    store.Store.SetAdapter(mockUsers, mockSubs, mockTopics, mockMessages, nil)
    store.RegisterAuthScheme("basic", func(_ []byte) (auth.AuthHandler, error) { return mockAuthHandler, nil })

    botUserID := "usrBotUser1"
    botUserUID := types.ParseUserId(botUserID)
    otherUserID := "usrOtherUserF"
    otherUserUID := types.ParseUserId(otherUserID)
    p2pTopicName := botUserUID.P2PName(otherUserUID)

    inputData := &Data{
        Users: []User{
            {Username: "botuser", Password: "(random)", State: "ok"}, // Bot user
            {Username: "otheruser", Password: "pw", State: "ok"},
        },
        P2psubs: []P2PSub{
            {Users: []P2PUser{{Name: "botuser"}, {Name: "otheruser"}}},
        },
        Forms: []map[string]interface{}{
            {"txt": "form 1 content"},
            {"txt": "form 2 content"},
        },
        Messages: []string{"initial message"}, // Need at least one message for seq id > 0
        datapath: ".",
    }

    // Mock setup
    mockAuthHandler.On("Init", mock.Anything, mock.Anything).Return(nil).Once()
    mockUsers.On("Create", mock.AnythingOfType("*types.User"), mock.Anything).Run(func(args mock.Arguments) {
        u := args.Get(0).(*types.User)
        if u.Tags[0] == "basic:botuser" { u.Id = botUserID; u.ObjHeader.SetUid(botUserUID) } else { u.Id = otherUserID; u.ObjHeader.SetUid(otherUserUID) }
    }).Return(mock.AnythingOfType("string"), nil).Twice()
    // Need to capture generated password for bot user to match AddRecord call
    var botPassword string
    mockAuthHandler.On("AddRecord", mock.MatchedBy(func(r *auth.Rec) bool { return r.Uid == botUserUID}), mock.MatchedBy(func(s []byte) bool { botPassword = strings.SplitN(string(s),":",2)[1]; return true}), "").Return("authBot", nil).Once()
    mockAuthHandler.On("AddRecord", mock.MatchedBy(func(r *auth.Rec) bool { return r.Uid == otherUserUID}), mock.Anything, "").Return("authOther", nil).Once()
    mockTopics.On("CreateP2P", mock.AnythingOfType("*types.Subscription"), mock.AnythingOfType("*types.Subscription")).Return(nil).Once()

    // Mock initial message save (single message path)
     mockMessages.On("Save", mock.MatchedBy(func(msg *types.Message) bool {
        return msg.Topic == p2pTopicName && msg.SeqId == 1 && msg.Content == "initial message"
    }), nil, true).Return(nil, 1).Once()


    // Mock Messages.Save for the forms
    expectedFormContent1 := map[string]interface{}{"txt": "form 1 content"}
    expectedFormContent2 := map[string]interface{}{"txt": "form 2 content"}
    expectedHeaders := types.MessageHeaders{"mime": "text/x-drafty"}

    // Form 1
    mockMessages.On("Save", mock.MatchedBy(func(msg *types.Message) bool {
        return msg.Topic == p2pTopicName && msg.From == botUserID && msg.SeqId == 2 &&
               assert.ObjectsAreEqual(expectedHeaders, msg.Head) &&
               assert.ObjectsAreEqual(expectedFormContent1, msg.Content)
    }), nil, true).Return(nil, 2).Once()
    // Form 2
    mockMessages.On("Save", mock.MatchedBy(func(msg *types.Message) bool {
        return msg.Topic == p2pTopicName && msg.From == botUserID && msg.SeqId == 3 &&
               assert.ObjectsAreEqual(expectedHeaders, msg.Head) &&
               assert.ObjectsAreEqual(expectedFormContent2, msg.Content)
    }), nil, true).Return(nil, 3).Once()

    // Act
    genDb(inputData)

    // Assert
    mockAuthHandler.AssertExpectations(t)
    mockUsers.AssertExpectations(t)
    mockTopics.AssertExpectations(t)
    mockSubs.AssertExpectations(t)
    mockMessages.AssertExpectations(t)

    // Cleanup
    store.Store = nil
    delete(auth.Available, "basic")

import (

	"path/filepath"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

Test Implementation:
func TestParsePublic_Scenarios_B1B(t *testing.T) {
    // Setup: Create a temporary directory and a dummy photo file
    tmpDir, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "testParsePublic")
    require.NoError(t, err)
    defer os.RemoveAll(tmpDir)

    photoFileName := "test.jpg"
    photoFilePath := filepath.Join(tmpDir, photoFileName)
    photoData := []byte("dummy photo data")
    err = os.WriteFile(photoFilePath, photoData, 0644)
    require.NoError(t, err)

    // Scenario 1: Both Fn and Photo empty
    cardInput1 := &theCard{}
    result1 := parsePublic(cardInput1, tmpDir)
    assert.Nil(t, result1, "Should return nil when both fn and photo are empty")

    // Scenario 2: Fn only
    cardInput2 := &theCard{Fn: "Just Name"}
    result2 := parsePublic(cardInput2, tmpDir)
    require.NotNil(t, result2)
    assert.Equal(t, "Just Name", result2.Fn)
    assert.Nil(t, result2.Photo, "Photo should be nil when only Fn is provided")

    // Scenario 3: Photo only (using path from argument)
    cardInput3 := &theCard{Photo: photoFileName, Type: "image/jpeg"}
    result3 := parsePublic(cardInput3, tmpDir)
    require.NotNil(t, result3)
    assert.Empty(t, result3.Fn, "Fn should be empty")
    require.NotNil(t, result3.Photo)
    assert.Equal(t, "image/jpeg", result3.Photo.Type)
    assert.Equal(t, photoData, result3.Photo.Data)

    // Scenario 4: Photo only (using path embedded in filename - simulating no leading slash)
    cardInput4 := &theCard{Photo: photoFileName, Type: "image/png"} // Use filename relative to tmpDir
    result4 := parsePublic(cardInput4, tmpDir) // Provide base path
    require.NotNil(t, result4)
    require.NotNil(t, result4.Photo)
    assert.Equal(t, "image/png", result4.Photo.Type)
    assert.Equal(t, photoData, result4.Photo.Data)

    // Scenario 5: Both Fn and Photo
    cardInput5 := &theCard{Fn: "Full Name", Photo: photoFileName, Type: "image/gif"}
    result5 := parsePublic(cardInput5, tmpDir)
    require.NotNil(t, result5)
    assert.Equal(t, "Full Name", result5.Fn)
    require.NotNil(t, result5.Photo)
    assert.Equal(t, "image/gif", result5.Photo.Type)
    assert.Equal(t, photoData, result5.Photo.Data)

    // Scenario 6: Photo with directory specified (absolute path)
    cardInput6 := &theCard{Photo: photoFilePath, Type: "image/bmp"} // Use absolute path
    result6 := parsePublic(cardInput6, "/different/path/ignored") // Base path should be ignored
    require.NotNil(t, result6)
    require.NotNil(t, result6.Photo)
    assert.Equal(t, "image/bmp", result6.Photo.Type)
    assert.Equal(t, photoData, result6.Photo.Data)
}

import (

	"google.golang.org/api/googleapi"

Test Implementation:
func TestDecodeGoogleApiError_UnknownDetailType_555(t *testing.T) {
	googleErr := &googleapi.Error{
		Code:    400,
		Message: "Bad Request",
		Details: []interface{}{
			map[string]interface{}{
				"@type": "unknown.type/SomeErrorDetail", // Unknown type
				"info":  "some additional info",
			},
			map[string]interface{}{ // Add a valid one to ensure it's processed if present
				"@type":     "type.googleapis.com/google.firebase.fcm.v1.FcmError",
				"errorCode": string(ErrorInvalidArgument),
			},
		},
	}
	decoded, errs := DecodeGoogleApiError(googleErr)
	assert.Equal(t, 400, decoded.HttpCode)
	assert.Equal(t, "Bad Request", decoded.ErrMessage)
	// FcmErrCode should be set by the valid detail item, not the unknown one.
	assert.Equal(t, string(ErrorInvalidArgument), decoded.FcmErrCode)
	assert.Empty(t, errs, "Should be no errors from processing details of unknown or valid types")

	// Test case with only unknown detail type
	googleErrOnlyUnknown := &googleapi.Error{
		Code:    400,
		Message: "Bad Request",
		Details: []interface{}{
			map[string]interface{}{
				"@type": "unknown.type/SomeErrorDetail",
			},
		},
	}
	decodedOnlyUnknown, errsOnlyUnknown := DecodeGoogleApiError(googleErrOnlyUnknown)
	assert.Equal(t, 400, decodedOnlyUnknown.HttpCode)
	assert.Equal(t, "Bad Request", decodedOnlyUnknown.ErrMessage)
	assert.Equal(t, string(ErrorUnspecified), decodedOnlyUnknown.FcmErrCode) // Defaults to Unspecified
	assert.Empty(t, errsOnlyUnknown, "Should be no errors from processing details of unknown type")
}

func TestDecodeGoogleApiError_InvalidOrMissingErrorCode_666(t *testing.T) {

		Details: []interface{}{

func TestMain_ResetFlagSuccess_812(t *testing.T) {
    // --- Mock setup ---
    originalStore := store.Store
    mockStore := new(storeMocks.Store)
    store.Store = mockStore
    defer func() { store.Store = originalStore }() // Restore

    // Mock os/log behavior
    var logOutput strings.Builder
    log.SetOutput(&logOutput)
    defer log.SetOutput(os.Stderr) // Restore log output

    mockExit := func(code int) {
        if code != 0 {
            panic(fmt.Sprintf("os.Exit called with %d", code))
        }
        // Do nothing for exit 0 to allow test completion
    }
    defer func(f func(int)) { osExit = f }(osExit)
    osExit = mockExit

    // Mock file operations
    mockOsOpen := func(name string) (*os.File, error) {
        if name == "./tinode.conf" {
            // Provide a minimal valid JSON config
            content := `{"store_config": {}}`
            tmpfile, err := ioutil.TempFile("", "config.*.json")
            require.NoError(t, err)
            _, err = tmpfile.WriteString(content)
            require.NoError(t, err)
            _, err = tmpfile.Seek(0, 0)
            require.NoError(t, err)
            // Don't close tmpfile here, os.Open returns an open file
            // The caller (main) is responsible for closing it implicitly via jsonco
            return tmpfile, nil
        }
        return nil, os.ErrNotExist
    }
    defer func(f func(string) (*os.File, error)) { osOpen = f }(osOpen)
    osOpen = mockOsOpen
    // No need to mock ioutil.ReadFile as --data is not used

    // --- Mock Store expectations ---
    confJson := json.RawMessage(`{}`)
    mockStore.On("Open", 1, confJson).Return(nil) // Assume DB exists initially
    mockStore.On("GetAdapterName").Return("mockdb")
    mockStore.On("GetAdapterVersion").Return(1)
    mockStore.On("GetDbVersion").Return(1).Maybe() // May or may not be called before InitDb
    mockStore.On("IsOpen").Return(true).Maybe()
    mockStore.On("InitDb", confJson, true).Return(nil) // Expect reset (drop=true)
    mockStore.On("Close").Return(nil)

    // --- Test execution ---
    // Simulate command line arguments
    os.Args = []string{"tinode-db", "--config=./tinode.conf", "--reset"}
    // Reset flags for this test run
    flag.CommandLine = flag.NewFlagSet(os.Args[0], flag.ExitOnError)

    // Run main
    main()

    // --- Assertions ---
    mockStore.AssertExpectations(t)
    // Check log output for expected messages
    logStr := logOutput.String()
    assert.Contains(t, logStr, "Reset requested. Dropping and recreating the database.")
    assert.Contains(t, logStr, "Database successfully reset.")
    assert.Contains(t, logStr, "All done.")
    // Ensure no fatal errors occurred (would panic due to mockExit)
}

func TestMain_AddRootSuccess_441(t *testing.T) {
    // --- Mock setup ---
    originalStore := store.Store
    originalUsers := store.Users
    mockStore := new(storeMocks.Store)
    mockUsers := new(storeMocks.Users)
    mockAuthHandler := new(authMocks.AuthHandler)
    store.Store = mockStore
    store.Users = mockUsers // Inject mock Users adapter
    defer func() {
        store.Store = originalStore
        store.Users = originalUsers
    }()

    var logOutput strings.Builder
    log.SetOutput(&logOutput)
    defer log.SetOutput(os.Stderr)

    mockExit := func(code int) {
        if code != 0 {
            panic(fmt.Sprintf("os.Exit called with %d", code))
        }
    }
    defer func(f func(int)) { osExit = f }(osExit)
    osExit = mockExit

    mockOsOpen := func(name string) (*os.File, error) {
        if name == "./tinode.conf" {
            content := `{"store_config": {}}`
            tmpfile, err := ioutil.TempFile("", "config.*.json")
            require.NoError(t, err)
            _, err = tmpfile.WriteString(content)
            require.NoError(t, err)
            _, err = tmpfile.Seek(0, 0)
            require.NoError(t, err)
            return tmpfile, nil
        }
        return nil, os.ErrNotExist
    }
    defer func(f func(string) (*os.File, error)) { osOpen = f }(osOpen)
    osOpen = mockOsOpen

    // --- Mock Store/Users/Auth expectations ---
    confJson := json.RawMessage(`{}`)
    rootUname := "newroot"
    rootPassword := "securepass123"
    rootArg := rootUname + ":" + rootPassword
    expectedPassBytes := []byte(rootUname + ":" + rootPassword)

    mockStore.On("Open", 1, confJson).Return(nil)
    mockStore.On("GetAdapterName").Return("mockdb")
    mockStore.On("GetAdapterVersion").Return(1)
    mockStore.On("GetDbVersion").Return(1).Maybe()
    mockStore.On("IsOpen").Return(true).Maybe()
    mockStore.On("GetAuthHandler", "basic").Return(mockAuthHandler)
    mockStore.On("Close").Return(nil)

    // Capture the user being created
    var createdUser *types.User
    mockUsers.On("Create", mock.AnythingOfType("*types.User"), mock.Anything).Run(func(args mock.Arguments) {
        createdUser = args.Get(0).(*types.User)
        // Simulate successful creation by setting a UID
        createdUser.ObjHeader.SetUid(types.ParseUserId("usr" + store.Store.GetUidString()))
    }).Return(nil, nil) // First call in main() -> Create

    // Expect AddRecord with the created user's UID
    mockAuthHandler.On("AddRecord", mock.MatchedBy(func(rec *auth.Rec) bool {
        return rec.Uid == createdUser.Uid() && rec.AuthLevel == auth.LevelRoot
    }), expectedPassBytes, "").Return(&auth.Rec{}, nil)

    // --- Test execution ---
    os.Args = []string{"tinode-db", "--config=./tinode.conf", "--add_root=" + rootArg}
    flag.CommandLine = flag.NewFlagSet(os.Args[0], flag.ExitOnError)

    main()

    // --- Assertions ---
    mockStore.AssertExpectations(t)
    mockUsers.AssertExpectations(t)
    mockAuthHandler.AssertExpectations(t)

    logStr := logOutput.String()
    assert.Contains(t, logStr, "Database exists, version is correct.")
    assert.Contains(t, logStr, fmt.Sprintf("ROOT user created: '%s:%s'", rootUname, rootPassword))
    assert.Contains(t, logStr, "All done.")
}

        fatalCalled = true
        panic("log.Fatal called") // Stop execution like log.Fatal
    }
    defer func(f func(...interface{})) { logFatalf = f }(logFatalf)
    logFatalf = mockFatal

    mockOsOpen := func(name string) (*os.File, error) {
        if name == "./tinode.conf" {
            // Invalid JSON structure for StoreConfig (string instead of object)
            content := `{"store_config": "invalid"}`
            tmpfile, err := ioutil.TempFile("", "config.*.json")
            require.NoError(t, err)
            _, err = tmpfile.WriteString(content)
            require.NoError(t, err)
            _, err = tmpfile.Seek(0, 0)
            require.NoError(t, err)
            return tmpfile, nil
        }
        return nil, os.ErrNotExist
    }
    defer func(f func(string) (*os.File, error)) { osOpen = f }(osOpen)
    osOpen = mockOsOpen

    // --- Test execution ---
    os.Args = []string{"tinode-db", "--config=./tinode.conf"}
    flag.CommandLine = flag.NewFlagSet(os.Args[0], flag.ContinueOnError) // Continue on error for testing flags

    // Expect main to panic because log.Fatal is mocked to panic
    assert.PanicsWithValue(t, "log.Fatal called", func() {
        main()
    }, "main should panic due to mocked log.Fatal")

    // --- Assertions ---
    assert.True(t, fatalCalled, "log.Fatalf should have been called")
    logStr := logOutput.String()
    // Check for specific parts of the expected UnmarshalTypeError message
    assert.Contains(t, logStr, "Unmarshall error in config file")
    assert.Contains(t, logStr, "store_config") // Field name
    assert.Contains(t, logStr, "json: cannot unmarshal string into Go value of type json.RawMessage")
}

    influxDBVersion := "2.0"
    pushBaseAddress := "http://localhost:8086"
    organization := "test-org"
    bucket := "test-bucket"
    token := "test-token"
    instance := "test-instance"

    exporter := NewInfluxDBExporter(influxDBVersion, pushBaseAddress, organization, bucket, token, instance, mockScr)

    expectedTargetAddress := "http://localhost:8086/api/v2/write?bucket=test-bucket&org=test-org"

Test Implementation:
func TestPush_Success_Corrected_242(t *testing.T) {
    // --- Arrange ---
    mockScr := new(mockScraper) // Use the defined mockScraper
    metrics := map[string]interface{}{
        "live_connections": float64(150.0),
        "request_latency": &histogram{ // Ensure histogram struct is defined
            count:   100,
            sum:     550.5,
            buckets: map[float64]uint64{0.1: 20, 0.5: 50, 1.0: 30},
        },
    }
    mockScr.On("CollectRaw").Return(metrics, nil)

    exporter := &InfluxDBExporter{
        targetAddress: "http://fake-influx:8086/api/v2/write?bucket=b&org=o",
        tokenHeader:   "Token fake-token",
        instance:      "test-instance-1",
        scraper:       mockScr, // Assign the mock scraper
    }

    // Mock HTTP client
    mockRT := &mockRoundTripper{}
    requestReceived := false
    mockRT.RoundTripFunc = func(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
        requestReceived = true
        // Assert request details
        assert.Equal(t, "POST", req.Method)
        assert.Equal(t, exporter.targetAddress, req.URL.String())
        assert.Equal(t, exporter.tokenHeader, req.Header.Get("Authorization"))

        bodyBytes, err := ioutil.ReadAll(req.Body)
        require.NoError(t, err)
        bodyString := string(bodyBytes)

        // Check if metrics are present (order independent)
        assert.Contains(t, bodyString, "live_connections,instance=test-instance-1 value=150.000000 ")
        assert.Contains(t, bodyString, "request_latency,instance=test-instance-1 count=100 ")
        assert.Contains(t, bodyString, "request_latency,instance=test-instance-1 sum=550.500000 ")
        // Check buckets specifically, format needs float ("le=%f")
        assert.Contains(t, bodyString, fmt.Sprintf("request_latency,instance=test-instance-1 le=%f,value=20 ", 0.1))
        assert.Contains(t, bodyString, fmt.Sprintf("request_latency,instance=test-instance-1 le=%f,value=50 ", 0.5))
        assert.Contains(t, bodyString, fmt.Sprintf("request_latency,instance=test-instance-1 le=%f,value=30 ", 1.0))


        // Check timestamps (allow small variation, check only one line)
        lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(bodyString), "\n")
        require.NotEmpty(t, lines)
        parts := strings.Fields(lines[0])
        require.True(t, len(parts) >= 3)
        ts, err := strconv.ParseInt(parts[len(parts)-1], 10, 64)
        require.NoError(t, err)
        assert.InDelta(t, time.Now().UnixNano(), ts, float64(5*time.Second)) // Allow 5 sec diff

        // Return success response
        return &http.Response{
            StatusCode: http.StatusOK, // Changed to StatusOK (200) for success
            Status:     "200 OK",      // Added Status field
            Body:       ioutil.NopCloser(strings.NewReader("")),
            Header:     make(http.Header),
        }, nil
    }
    originalClient := http.DefaultClient
    http.DefaultClient = &http.Client{Transport: mockRT}
    defer func() { http.DefaultClient = originalClient }() // Restore original client

    // --- Act ---
    err := exporter.Push()

    // --- Assert ---
    assert.NoError(t, err)
    assert.True(t, requestReceived, "http.DefaultClient.Do was not called")
    mockScr.AssertExpectations(t)
}

func TestPromExporter_Collect_ValidScrape_Fixed_789(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    server := "http://localhost:6060" // Use a port likely unused
    namespace := "tinode_test"
    timeout := 1 * time.Second
    mockScraper := new(MockScraper) // Use the defined mock
    exporter := NewPromExporter(server, namespace, timeout, mockScraper)
    ch := make(chan prometheus.Metric, 100) // Buffered channel

    stats := map[string]interface{}{
        "Version":                      "0.17.0", // String version needs special handling if parseNumeric expects float
        "LiveTopics":                   5.0,
        "TotalTopics":                  100.0,
        "LiveSessions":                 10.0,
        "TotalSessions":                200.0,
        "NumGoroutines":                50.0,
        "IncomingMessagesWebsockTotal": 1000.0,
        "OutgoingMessagesWebsockTotal": 900.0,
        "IncomingMessagesLongpollTotal": 50.0,
        "OutgoingMessagesLongpollTotal": 40.0,
        "IncomingMessagesGrpcTotal":     10.0,
        "OutgoingMessagesGrpcTotal":     5.0,
        "FileDownloadsTotal":           20.0,
        "FileUploadsTotal":             15.0,
        "CtrlCodesTotal2xx":            500.0,
        "CtrlCodesTotal3xx":            10.0,
        "CtrlCodesTotal4xx":            5.0,
        "CtrlCodesTotal5xx":            1.0,
        "ClusterLeader":                1.0, // Assuming 1 means true
        "TotalClusterNodes":            3.0,
        "LiveClusterNodes":             2.0,
        "memstats.Alloc":               1024000.0,
        "RequestLatency": map[string]interface{}{ // Histogram data
            "count": uint64(100),
            "sum":   float64(5000),
            "buckets": map[float64]uint64{
                10:  10,
                50:  30,
                100: 50,
                500: 10,
            },
        },
        "OutgoingMessageSize": map[string]interface{}{ // Histogram data
            "count": uint64(960), // Sum of outgoing messages
            "sum":   float64(1024 * 500), // Example sum of bytes
            "buckets": map[float64]uint64{
                128:  200,
                512:  400,
                1024: 300,
                4096: 60,
            },
        },
    }

    // Mock the behavior of parseNumeric and parseHisto for this test
    // We need these because they are likely in a separate file (utils.go)
    originalParseNumeric := parseNumeric
    originalParseHisto := parseHisto
    defer func() {
        parseNumeric = originalParseNumeric
        parseHisto = originalParseHisto
    }()

    parseNumeric = func(stats map[string]interface{}, key string) (float64, error) {
        // Special handling for Version which is string in stats but gauge in Prometheus
        if key == "Version" {
             _, ok := stats[key].(string)
             if !ok {
                 return 0, fmt.Errorf("key '%s' is not a string", key)
             }
            // Represent version presence as 1.0 for gauge
            return 1.0, nil
        }
        val, ok := stats[key]
        if !ok {
            return 0, fmt.Errorf("key '%s' not found", key)
        }
        fVal, ok := val.(float64)
        if !ok {
             // Try int conversion for Prometheus compatibility
             if iVal, okInt := val.(int); okInt {
                  return float64(iVal), nil
             }
             if iVal, okInt64 := val.(int64); okInt64 {
                 return float64(iVal), nil
             }
            return 0, fmt.Errorf("value for key '%s' is not float64: %T", key, val)
        }
        return fVal, nil
    }

    parseHisto = func(stats map[string]interface{}, key string) (histogramData, error) {
         val, ok := stats[key]
         if !ok {
             return histogramData{}, fmt.Errorf("key '%s' not found", key)
         }
         hMap, ok := val.(map[string]interface{})
         if !ok {
             return histogramData{}, fmt.Errorf("value for key '%s' is not a map", key)
         }

         count, ok := hMap["count"].(uint64)
         if !ok { return histogramData{}, fmt.Errorf("histo key '%s': count invalid", key)}
         sum, ok := hMap["sum"].(float64)
         if !ok { return histogramData{}, fmt.Errorf("histo key '%s': sum invalid", key)}
         bucketsRaw, ok := hMap["buckets"].(map[float64]uint64)
          if !ok {
              // Try converting map[string]interface{} to map[float64]uint64
               bucketsMapStr, okStr := hMap["buckets"].(map[string]interface{})
               if !okStr {
                   return histogramData{}, fmt.Errorf("histo key '%s': buckets invalid type", key)
               }
               bucketsRaw = make(map[float64]uint64)
               for k, v := range bucketsMapStr {
                   fKey, err := strconv.ParseFloat(k, 64)
                   if err != nil {
                       return histogramData{}, fmt.Errorf("histo key '%s': bucket key '%s' invalid float", key, k)
                   }
                   uiVal, okUint := v.(uint64)
                   if !okUint {
                        // try int conversion
                         iVal, okInt := v.(int)
                         if !okInt {
                           return histogramData{}, fmt.Errorf("histo key '%s': bucket value '%v' invalid uint64", key, v)
                         }
                         uiVal = uint64(iVal)
                   }
                   bucketsRaw[fKey] = uiVal
               }
          }

         return histogramData{count: count, sum: sum, buckets: bucketsRaw}, nil
    }


    mockScraper.On("Scrape").Return(stats, nil).Once()

    // Act: Run Collect in the main goroutine for simplicity in testing channel reads
    exporter.Collect(ch)
    close(ch) // Close channel after Collect finishes

    // Assert
    collectedMetrics := []prometheus.Metric{}
    metricMap := make(map[string]prometheus.Metric) // To easily check metric presence

    for metric := range ch {
        collectedMetrics = append(collectedMetrics, metric)
        // Use String() representation which includes FQName
         descStr := metric.Desc().String()
         // Extract FQName (hacky but effective for testing)
         fqNameStart := strings.Index(descStr, "fqName: \"") + len("fqName: \"")
         fqNameEnd := strings.Index(descStr[fqNameStart:], "\"")
         fqName := descStr[fqNameStart : fqNameStart+fqNameEnd]
         metricMap[fqName] = metric
    }

    require.Greater(t, len(collectedMetrics), 20, "Should collect multiple metrics + 'up'") // Check we got more than just 'up'

    // Check 'up' metric specifically
    upMetric, ok := metricMap[namespace+"_up"]
    require.True(t, ok, "up metric should be present")
    // Helper to extract gauge value
    gaugeValue := func(m prometheus.Metric) float64 {
        var writtenMetric dto.Metric
        m.Write(&writtenMetric)
        return *writtenMetric.Gauge.Value
    }
    assert.Equal(t, 1.0, gaugeValue(upMetric), "'up' metric should be 1.0 on success")

    // Verify other metrics were generated (presence check is sufficient here)
    expectedMetrics := []string{
            namespace + "_version", namespace + "_topics_live_count", namespace + "_topics_total",
            namespace + "_sessions_live_count", namespace + "_sessions_total", namespace + "_num_goroutines",
            namespace + "_incoming_messages_websock_total", namespace + "_outgoing_messages_websock_total",
            namespace + "_incoming_messages_longpoll_total", namespace + "_outgoing_messages_longpoll_total",
            namespace + "_incoming_messages_grpc_total", namespace + "_outgoing_messages_grpc_total",
            namespace + "_file_downloads_total", namespace + "_file_uploads_total",
            namespace + "_ctrl_codes_total_2xx", namespace + "_ctrl_codes_total_3xx",
            namespace + "_ctrl_codes_total_4xx", namespace + "_ctrl_codes_total_5xx",
            namespace + "_cluster_leader", namespace + "_cluster_size", namespace + "_cluster_nodes_live",
            namespace + "_malloced_bytes", namespace + "_request_latency_ms_count", namespace+"_outgoing_message_bytes",
    }
    for _, name := range expectedMetrics {
        _, ok := metricMap[name]
        assert.True(t, ok, "Expected metric %s to be present", name)
    }


    mockScraper.AssertExpectations(t)
}

func TestParseStats_NumericParseError_404(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    namespace := "tinode_test_ps_num_err"
    exporter := NewPromExporter("", namespace, 0, nil)
    ch := make(chan prometheus.Metric, 50) // Buffer needed

    stats := map[string]interface{}{
        "Version":      "0.17.3",
        "LiveTopics":   "not-a-number", // Invalid numeric value
        "TotalTopics":  100.0,
        // ... other stats can be present or absent, the first error matters
    }

    // Mock parseNumeric to fail for "LiveTopics"
    originalParseNumeric := parseNumeric
    defer func() { parseNumeric = originalParseNumeric }()
    parseNumeric = func(s map[string]interface{}, key string) (float64, error) {
        if key == "LiveTopics" {
            return 0, errors.New("cannot parse 'not-a-number'")
        }
        if key == "Version" { return 1.0, nil } // Version needs to "succeed" to reach LiveTopics
        v, ok := s[key]
        if !ok { return 0, fmt.Errorf("missing key: %s", key) }
        fv, ok := v.(float64)
        if !ok { return 0, fmt.Errorf("not float64: %s", key) }
        return fv, nil
    }
     // Mock parseHisto to prevent panic if reached
     originalParseHisto := parseHisto
     defer func() { parseHisto = originalParseHisto }()
     parseHisto = func(map[string]interface{}, string) (histogramData, error) {
         return histogramData{}, nil
     }

    // Act
    err := exporter.parseStats(ch, stats)
    // Don't close channel immediately, read any potential metrics first
    // (though on first error, it should stop sending)
    close(ch)

    // Assert
    require.Error(t, err, "parseStats should return the first error encountered")
    assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "cannot parse 'not-a-number'", "Error message should reflect the parsing failure")

    // Check that few or no metrics were sent before the error
    metricCount := 0
    for range ch {
        metricCount++
    }
    // Only metrics before the failing one might be sent. Version would be sent.
    assert.LessOrEqual(t, metricCount, 1, "Should stop sending metrics after the first error")
}

func TestParseAndUpdateHisto_Success_808(t *testing.T) {

    namespace := "test_pauh_succ"
    exporter := NewPromExporter("", namespace, 0, nil)
    ch := make(chan prometheus.Metric, 1)
    desc := exporter.requestLatencyMsCount // Use histogram descriptor
    stats := map[string]interface{}{
        "Latency": map[string]interface{}{"dummy": "data"}, // Content doesn't matter due to mock
    }
    key := "Latency"
    expectedHistoData := histogramData{
        count:   10,
        sum:     55.5,
        buckets: map[float64]uint64{10: 2, 50: 3, 100: 5},
    }

    // Mock parseHisto for this isolated test
    originalParseHisto := parseHisto
    defer func() { parseHisto = originalParseHisto }()
    parseHisto = func(s map[string]interface{}, k string) (histogramData, error) {
        require.Equal(t, key, k)
        require.Equal(t, stats, s)
        return expectedHistoData, nil
    }

    // Act
    err := exporter.parseAndUpdateHisto(ch, desc, stats, key)
    close(ch)

    // Assert

    require.Len(t, ch, 1, "Should have sent one histogram metric")

    metric := <-ch

    // Verify histogram metric content

    assert.Equal(t, expectedHistoData.sum, *writtenMetric.Histogram.SampleSum)

    // Check buckets (ordering might vary, so check presence and value)
    receivedBuckets := make(map[float64]uint64)
    for _, b := range writtenMetric.Histogram.Bucket {
        receivedBuckets[*b.UpperBound] = *b.CumulativeCount
    }
    assert.Equal(t, expectedHistoData.buckets, receivedBuckets)
}

Test Implementation:
func TestDecodeGoogleApiError_DetailMapMissingType_721(t *testing.T) {
    googleErr := &googleapi.Error{
        Code:    400,
        Message: "Bad Request",
        Details: []interface{}{
            map[string]interface{}{ // Missing '@type' key
                "someKey": "someValue",
            },
            map[string]interface{}{ // Valid FcmError detail
                "@type":     "type.googleapis.com/google.firebase.fcm.v1.FcmError",
                "errorCode": string(ErrorInvalidArgument),
            },
        },
    }
    decoded, errs := DecodeGoogleApiError(googleErr)
    assert.Equal(t, 400, decoded.HttpCode)
    assert.Equal(t, "Bad Request", decoded.ErrMessage)
    // FcmErrCode should be set by the valid detail
    assert.Equal(t, ErrorInvalidArgument, decoded.FcmErrCode)
    assert.Empty(t, errs, "Should be no errors reported for missing @type")

    // Case 2: Only details with missing '@type'
    googleErrOnlyMissingType := &googleapi.Error{
        Code:    400,
        Message: "Bad Request Only Missing Type",
        Details: []interface{}{
            map[string]interface{}{"key1": "val1"}, // Missing '@type'
            map[string]interface{}{"key2": "val2"}, // Missing '@type'
        },
    }
    decoded2, errs2 := DecodeGoogleApiError(googleErrOnlyMissingType)
    assert.Equal(t, 400, decoded2.HttpCode)
    assert.Equal(t, "Bad Request Only Missing Type", decoded2.ErrMessage)
    // FcmErrCode should default as no valid FcmError detail was found
    assert.Equal(t, ErrorUnspecified, decoded2.FcmErrCode)
    assert.Empty(t, errs2)
}

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

Test Implementation:
func TestParseHisto_Success_734(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    stats := map[string]interface{}{
        "histo.count":             10.0, // Note: JSON numbers decode to float64
        "histo.sum":               100.0,
        "histo.count_per_bucket": []interface{}{1.0, 2.0, 7.0}, // Total count = 1+2+7 = 10
        "histo.bounds":           []interface{}{10.0, 20.0},    // Two bounds, expects 3 buckets
    }
    key := "histo"
    expectedBuckets := map[float64]uint64{
        10.0: 1, // Cumulative count for <= 10.0 (buckets[0])
        20.0: 3, // Cumulative count for <= 20.0 (buckets[0] + buckets[1])
        // +Inf bucket implicitly contains the remaining count (7.0)
    }

    // Act
    h, err := parseHisto(stats, key)

    // Assert
    require.NoError(t, err)
    require.NotNil(t, h)
    assert.Equal(t, uint64(10), h.count, "Histogram count mismatch")
    assert.Equal(t, 100.0, h.sum, "Histogram sum mismatch")
    assert.Equal(t, expectedBuckets, h.buckets, "Histogram buckets mismatch")
}

    require.True(t, ok, "histo1 metric should be of type *histogram")

        "CtrlCodesTotal4xx":            5.0,
        "CtrlCodesTotal5xx":            1.0,
        "ClusterLeader":                1.0, // Assuming 1.0 means true
        "TotalClusterNodes":            3.0,
        "LiveClusterNodes":             2.0,
        "memstats.Alloc":               1024000.0,
        "RequestLatency": map[string]interface{}{ // Data structure expected by parseHisto
            "count": uint64(100),
            "sum":   float64(5000.5),
            "buckets": map[string]interface{}{ // Keys might be strings from JSON unmarshal
                "10":  uint64(10), // Use uint64 for counts
                "50":  uint64(30),
                "100": uint64(50),
                "500": uint64(10),
             },
        },
        "OutgoingMessageSize": map[string]interface{}{ // Data structure expected by parseHisto
            "count": uint64(960),
            "sum":   float64(1024 * 512),
            "buckets": map[string]interface{}{
                "128":  uint64(200),
                "512":  uint64(400),
                "1024": uint64(300),
                "4096": uint64(60),
            },
        },
    }

    // Mock Scraper behavior
    mockScraper.On("Scrape").Return(stats, nil).Once()

    // Act
    exporter.Collect(ch)
    close(ch)

    // Assert
    metricMap := make(map[string]prometheus.Metric)
    for metric := range ch {
        var writtenMetric dto.Metric
        metric.Write(&writtenMetric)
        fqName := metric.Desc().fqName // Use internal field for unique key
        metricMap[fqName] = metric
    }

    // Check 'up' metric
    require.Contains(t, metricMap, namespace+"_up", "'up' metric missing")
    upMetric := metricMap[namespace+"_up"]
    var upDto dto.Metric
    upMetric.Write(&upDto)
    require.NotNil(t, upDto.Gauge)
    assert.Equal(t, 1.0, *upDto.Gauge.Value, "'up' should be 1.0 on success")
    delete(metricMap, namespace+"_up") // Remove 'up' for count check

    // Check total number of metrics (24 defined + 1 up)
    // Note: The "Version" gauge isn't explicitly created, parseAndUpdate handles it.
    // So we expect 24 metrics from parseStats + 1 'up' = 25 total.
    assert.Equal(t, 24, len(metricMap), "Expected 24 metrics from stats map")

    // Spot check a few metric values
    require.Contains(t, metricMap, namespace+"_topics_live_count")
    var topicsLiveDto dto.Metric
    metricMap[namespace+"_topics_live_count"].Write(&topicsLiveDto)
    require.NotNil(t, topicsLiveDto.Gauge)
    assert.Equal(t, 5.0, *topicsLiveDto.Gauge.Value)

    require.Contains(t, metricMap, namespace+"_sessions_total")
    var sessionsTotalDto dto.Metric
    metricMap[namespace+"_sessions_total"].Write(&sessionsTotalDto)
    require.NotNil(t, sessionsTotalDto.Counter)
    assert.Equal(t, 200.0, *sessionsTotalDto.Counter.Value)

    // Check histogram
    require.Contains(t, metricMap, namespace+"_request_latency_ms_count")
    var latencyHistoDto dto.Metric
    metricMap[namespace+"_request_latency_ms_count"].Write(&latencyHistoDto)
    require.NotNil(t, latencyHistoDto.Histogram)
    assert.Equal(t, uint64(100), *latencyHistoDto.Histogram.SampleCount)
    assert.Equal(t, 5000.5, *latencyHistoDto.Histogram.SampleSum)
    assert.Len(t, latencyHistoDto.Histogram.Bucket, 4, "Expected 4 buckets")

    // Verify mock expectations
    mockScraper.AssertExpectations(t)
}

    // Arrange
    mockScr := &Scraper{} // Use a pointer to Scraper
    influxDBVersion := "2.0"
    pushBaseAddress := "http://localhost:8086"
    organization := "test-org"
    bucket := "test-bucket"
    token := "test-token"
    instance := "test-instance"

    // Act
    exporter := NewInfluxDBExporter(influxDBVersion, pushBaseAddress, organization, bucket, token, instance, mockScr)

    // Assert
    require.NotNil(t, exporter)
    // Expected URL format for v2.0
    expectedTargetAddress := "http://localhost:8086/api/v2/write?bucket=test-bucket&org=test-org"
    parsedExpected, _ := url.Parse(expectedTargetAddress)
    parsedActual, _ := url.Parse(exporter.targetAddress)

    // Compare URLs ignoring query parameter order by comparing parsed query values
    assert.Equal(t, parsedExpected.Scheme, parsedActual.Scheme)
    assert.Equal(t, parsedExpected.Host, parsedActual.Host)
    assert.Equal(t, parsedExpected.Path, parsedActual.Path) // Check path
    assert.Equal(t, parsedExpected.Query(), parsedActual.Query())


    // Expected header format for v2.0
    assert.Equal(t, "Token test-token", exporter.tokenHeader)
    assert.Equal(t, organization, exporter.organization)
    assert.Equal(t, bucket, exporter.bucket)
    assert.Equal(t, instance, exporter.instance)
    assert.Equal(t, mockScr, exporter.scraper) // Check scraper assignment
}

Test Implementation:
func TestPush_Success_242(t *testing.T) {
    // --- Arrange ---
    mockScr := new(mockScraper)
    metrics := map[string]interface{}{
        "live_connections": float64(150.0),
        "request_latency": &histogram{ // Ensure histogram struct matches definition
            count:   100,
            sum:     550.5,
            buckets: map[float64]uint64{0.1: 20, 0.5: 50, 1.0: 30},
        },
    }
    mockScr.On("CollectRaw").Return(metrics, nil)

    exporter := &InfluxDBExporter{
        targetAddress: "http://fake-influx:8086/api/v2/write?bucket=b&org=o",
        tokenHeader:   "Token fake-token",
        instance:      "test-instance-1",
        scraper:       mockScr, // Assign the mock scraper
    }

    // Mock HTTP client
    mockRT := &mockRoundTripper{}
    requestReceived := false
    mockRT.RoundTripFunc = func(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
        requestReceived = true
        // Assert request details
        assert.Equal(t, "POST", req.Method)
        assert.Equal(t, exporter.targetAddress, req.URL.String())
        assert.Equal(t, exporter.tokenHeader, req.Header.Get("Authorization"))

        bodyBytes, err := io.ReadAll(req.Body) // Use io.ReadAll
        require.NoError(t, err)
        bodyString := string(bodyBytes)

        // Check if metrics are present (order independent)
        assert.Contains(t, bodyString, "live_connections,instance=test-instance-1 value=150.000000 ")
        assert.Contains(t, bodyString, "request_latency,instance=test-instance-1 count=100 ")
        assert.Contains(t, bodyString, "request_latency,instance=test-instance-1 sum=550.500000 ")
        // Check buckets specifically, format needs float ("le=%f")
        assert.Contains(t, bodyString, fmt.Sprintf("request_latency,instance=test-instance-1 le=%f,value=20 ", 0.1))
        assert.Contains(t, bodyString, fmt.Sprintf("request_latency,instance=test-instance-1 le=%f,value=50 ", 0.5))
        assert.Contains(t, bodyString, fmt.Sprintf("request_latency,instance=test-instance-1 le=%f,value=30 ", 1.0))


        // Check timestamps (allow small variation, check only one line)
        lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(bodyString), "\n")
        require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(lines), 3) // Ensure enough lines for histogram
        parts := strings.Fields(lines[0])
        require.True(t, len(parts) >= 3)
        ts, err := strconv.ParseInt(parts[len(parts)-1], 10, 64)
        require.NoError(t, err)
        assert.InDelta(t, time.Now().UnixNano(), ts, float64(5*time.Second)) // Allow 5 sec diff

        // Return success response
        return &http.Response{
            StatusCode: http.StatusOK, // Use StatusOK
            Status:     "200 OK",      // Add Status field
            Body:       io.NopCloser(strings.NewReader("")), // Use io.NopCloser
            Header:     make(http.Header),
        }, nil
    }
    originalClient := http.DefaultClient
    http.DefaultClient = &http.Client{Transport: mockRT}
    defer func() { http.DefaultClient = originalClient }() // Restore original client

    // --- Act ---
    err := exporter.Push()

    // --- Assert ---
    assert.NoError(t, err)
    assert.True(t, requestReceived, "http.DefaultClient.Do was not called")
    mockScr.AssertExpectations(t)
}

func TestPush_HTTPResponseError_575(t *testing.T) {
    // --- Arrange ---
    mockScr := new(mockScraper)
    metrics := map[string]interface{}{"metric": float64(2.0)}
    mockScr.On("CollectRaw").Return(metrics, nil)

    exporter := &InfluxDBExporter{
        targetAddress: "http://fake-influx:8086/api/v2/write?bucket=b&org=o",
        tokenHeader:   "Token fake-token",
        instance:      "test-instance-3",
        scraper:       mockScr,
    }

    // Mock HTTP client to return a 400 Bad Request
    mockRT := &mockRoundTripper{}
    responseBody := `{"code":"invalid","message":"unable to parse points"}`
    responseStatus := "400 Bad Request"
    responseStatusCode := http.StatusBadRequest

    mockRT.RoundTripFunc = func(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
        // Assert request details
        assert.Equal(t, "POST", req.Method)
        assert.Equal(t, exporter.targetAddress, req.URL.String())
        return &http.Response{
            StatusCode: responseStatusCode,
            Status:     responseStatus,
            Body:       io.NopCloser(strings.NewReader(responseBody)),
            Header:     make(http.Header),
        }, nil
    }
    originalClient := http.DefaultClient
    http.DefaultClient = &http.Client{Transport: mockRT}
    defer func() { http.DefaultClient = originalClient }()

    // --- Act ---
    err := exporter.Push()

    // --- Assert ---
    require.Error(t, err)
    expectedErrorMsg := fmt.Sprintf("HTTP %s: %s", responseStatus, responseBody)
    assert.EqualError(t, err, expectedErrorMsg)
    mockScr.AssertExpectations(t)
}

Test Implementation:
func TestPush_HTTPResponseError_BodyReadError_686(t *testing.T) {
    // --- Arrange ---
    mockScr := new(mockScraper)
    metrics := map[string]interface{}{"metric": float64(3.0)}
    mockScr.On("CollectRaw").Return(metrics, nil)

    exporter := &InfluxDBExporter{
        targetAddress: "http://fake-influx:8086/api/v2/write?bucket=b&org=o",
        tokenHeader:   "Token fake-token",
        instance:      "test-instance-4",
        scraper:       mockScr,
    }

    // Mock HTTP client to return a 500 Internal Server Error with a faulty body reader
    mockRT := &mockRoundTripper{}
    responseStatus := "500 Internal Server Error"
    responseStatusCode := http.StatusInternalServerError
    bodyReadError := fmt.Errorf("failed to read response body")

    // Create a reader that returns an error on Read
    errorReader := &mockReader{ReadFunc: func(p []byte) (n int, err error) {
        return 0, bodyReadError
    }}

    mockRT.RoundTripFunc = func(req *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
        assert.Equal(t, "POST", req.Method)
        assert.Equal(t, exporter.targetAddress, req.URL.String())
        return &http.Response{
            StatusCode: responseStatusCode,
            Status:     responseStatus,
            Body:       io.NopCloser(errorReader), // Use the error reader
            Header:     make(http.Header),
        }, nil
    }
    originalClient := http.DefaultClient
    http.DefaultClient = &http.Client{Transport: mockRT}
    defer func() { http.DefaultClient = originalClient }()

    // --- Act ---
    err := exporter.Push()

    // --- Assert ---
    require.Error(t, err)
    // The error message should contain the status and the body read error
    expectedErrorMsg := fmt.Sprintf("HTTP %s: %s", responseStatus, bodyReadError.Error())
    assert.EqualError(t, err, expectedErrorMsg)
    mockScr.AssertExpectations(t)
}

func TestValidatorInit_ValidConfig_831(t *testing.T) {
	// Arrange
	v := &validator{}
	confJSON := `{
		"host_url": "http://localhost:6060",
		"languages": ["en", "es"],
		"universal_templ": "{{.Code}}",
		"sender": "+15005550006",
		"max_retries": 5,
		"code_length": 8,
		"twilio_conf": {}
	}`

	// Mock validate functions
	validate.MockValidateHostURL = func(origUrl string) (string, error) {
		assert.Equal(t, "http://localhost:6060", origUrl)
		return "http://localhost:6060", nil
	}
	validate.MockReadTemplateFile = func(pathTempl *textt.Template, lang string) (*textt.Template, string, error) {
		tmpl, _ := textt.New(lang).Parse("Template for " + lang)
		return tmpl, "path/to/" + lang, nil
	}
	defer func() {
		validate.MockValidateHostURL = nil
		validate.MockReadTemplateFile = nil
	}()

	mockTwilioInit = func(conf json.RawMessage) error {
		assert.NotNil(t, conf)
		return nil
	}
	defer func() { mockTwilioInit = nil }()


	// Act
	err := v.Init(confJSON)

	// Assert
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, "http://localhost:6060", v.HostUrl)
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"en", "es"}, v.Languages)
	assert.NotNil(t, v.universalTempl)
	assert.Len(t, v.universalTempl, 2)
	assert.NotNil(t, v.universalTempl[0])
	assert.NotNil(t, v.universalTempl[1])
	assert.NotNil(t, v.langMatcher)
	assert.Equal(t, "+15005550006", v.Sender)
	assert.Equal(t, 5, v.MaxRetries)
	assert.Equal(t, 8, v.CodeLength)
	expectedMaxCodeValue := big.NewInt(0).Exp(big.NewInt(10), big.NewInt(8), nil)
	assert.Equal(t, expectedMaxCodeValue, v.maxCodeValue)
	assert.NotNil(t, v.Twilio)
}
