func TestLargeFileServe_MediaHandlerHeadersStatusGet_312(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    ctrl, mockMediaHandler, _ := setupTestEnvironment(t)
    defer ctrl.Finish()

    // authHttpRequest is mocked to succeed by default in setup

    redirectHeaders := http.Header{"Location": []string{"/elsewhere"}}
    mockMediaHandler.EXPECT().Headers(gomock.Any(), true).Return(redirectHeaders, http.StatusFound, nil) // 302 Found

    req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/files/somefile", nil)
    req.Header.Set("X-Tinode-APIKey", "valid-key")
    require.NoError(t, err)
    recorder := httptest.NewRecorder()

    // Act
    largeFileServe(recorder, req)

    // Assert
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusFound, recorder.Code)
    assert.Equal(t, "/elsewhere", recorder.Header().Get("Location"))
    // Body should contain the status message for GET requests when handler terminates
    assert.Contains(t, recorder.Body.String(), http.StatusText(http.StatusFound))
    mockMediaHandler.AssertExpectations(t)
}

func TestLargeFileServe_MediaHandlerDownloadError_813(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    ctrl, mockMediaHandler, _ := setupTestEnvironment(t)
    defer ctrl.Finish()

    // authHttpRequest is mocked to succeed by default in setup

    mockMediaHandler.EXPECT().Headers(gomock.Any(), true).Return(http.Header{}, 0, nil) // Headers check passes
    expectedError := errors.New("download failed")
    mockMediaHandler.EXPECT().Download(gomock.Eq("/files/somefile")).Return(nil, nil, expectedError)

    req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/files/somefile", nil)
    req.Header.Set("X-Tinode-APIKey", "valid-key")
    require.NoError(t, err)
    recorder := httptest.NewRecorder()

    // Act
    largeFileServe(recorder, req)

    // Assert
    // Use the status code mapped by the mock decodeStoreError for "download failed"
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusNotFound, recorder.Code)
    assert.Contains(t, recorder.Body.String(), "Not Found")
    mockMediaHandler.AssertExpectations(t)
}

func TestLargeFileServe_GetSuccessHTMLAttachment_265(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    ctrl, mockMediaHandler, _ := setupTestEnvironment(t)
    defer ctrl.Finish()

    // authHttpRequest is mocked to succeed by default in setup

    fileContent := "<html><body>test</body></html>"
    mockReadSeeker := newMockReadSeekCloser(strings.NewReader(fileContent))
    fileDef := &types.FileDef{
        ObjHeader: types.ObjHeader{UpdatedAt: time.Now().Add(-time.Hour)}, // Access embedded field
        MimeType:  "text/html", // HTML mime type
    }

    mockMediaHandler.EXPECT().Headers(gomock.Any(), true).Return(http.Header{}, 0, nil)
    // Ensure the URL matches exactly, including query params if any
    mockMediaHandler.EXPECT().Download(gomock.Eq("/files/somefile.html")).Return(fileDef, mockReadSeeker, nil)

    req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/files/somefile.html", nil)
    req.Header.Set("X-Tinode-APIKey", "valid-key")
    require.NoError(t, err)
    recorder := httptest.NewRecorder()

    // Act
    largeFileServe(recorder, req)

    // Assert
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, recorder.Code)
    assert.Equal(t, "text/html", recorder.Header().Get("Content-Type"))
    assert.Equal(t, "attachment", recorder.Header().Get("Content-Disposition")) // Should be attachment for HTML
    assert.Equal(t, fileContent, recorder.Body.String())
    assert.True(t, mockReadSeeker.closed, "ReadSeekCloser should be closed")
    mockMediaHandler.AssertExpectations(t)
}

Test Implementation:
func TestLargeFileServe_GetSuccessImageInline_139(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    ctrl, mockMediaHandler, _ := setupTestEnvironment(t)
    defer ctrl.Finish()

    // authHttpRequest is mocked to succeed by default in setup

    fileContent := "imagedata"
    mockReadSeeker := newMockReadSeekCloser(strings.NewReader(fileContent))
    fileDef := &types.FileDef{
         ObjHeader: types.ObjHeader{UpdatedAt: time.Now().Add(-time.Hour)}, // Access embedded field
        MimeType:  "image/png", // Image mime type
    }

    mockMediaHandler.EXPECT().Headers(gomock.Any(), true).Return(http.Header{}, 0, nil)
    mockMediaHandler.EXPECT().Download(gomock.Eq("/files/image.png?asatt=false")).Return(fileDef, mockReadSeeker, nil)

    req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/files/image.png?asatt=false", nil) // Explicitly false
    req.Header.Set("X-Tinode-APIKey", "valid-key")
    require.NoError(t, err)
    recorder := httptest.NewRecorder()

    // Act
    largeFileServe(recorder, req)

    // Assert
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, recorder.Code)
    assert.Equal(t, "image/png", recorder.Header().Get("Content-Type"))
    // Note: ServeContent sets Content-Disposition to `inline` by default if filename is empty,
    // but browsers often treat it as empty. We check for empty or inline.
    contentDisposition := recorder.Header().Get("Content-Disposition")
    assert.True(t, contentDisposition == "" || contentDisposition == "inline", "Content-Disposition should be empty or inline")
    assert.Equal(t, fileContent, recorder.Body.String())
    assert.True(t, mockReadSeeker.closed, "ReadSeekCloser should be closed")
    mockMediaHandler.AssertExpectations(t)
}

func TestLargeFileReceive_PreflightOptionsSuccess_349(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    ctrl, mockMediaHandler, _ := setupTestEnvironment(t)
    defer ctrl.Finish()

    expectedHeaders := http.Header{"Access-Control-Allow-Methods": []string{"POST, PUT"}, "X-Upload-Limit": []string{"10MB"}}
    mockMediaHandler.EXPECT().Headers(gomock.Any(), false).Return(expectedHeaders, http.StatusNoContent, nil)

    req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodOptions, "/files/", nil)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    recorder := httptest.NewRecorder()

    // Act
    largeFileReceive(recorder, req)

    // Assert
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusNoContent, recorder.Code)
    assert.Equal(t, "POST, PUT", recorder.Header().Get("Access-Control-Allow-Methods"))
    assert.Equal(t, "10MB", recorder.Header().Get("X-Upload-Limit"))
    mockMediaHandler.AssertExpectations(t)
}

func TestLargeFileReceive_FileSizeExceeded_192(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    _, _, _ = setupTestEnvironment(t)

    originalMaxSize := globals.maxFileUploadSize
    globals.maxFileUploadSize = 10 // Set a small limit
    t.Cleanup(func() { globals.maxFileUploadSize = originalMaxSize })

    // Create a multipart body larger than the limit
    body := new(bytes.Buffer)
    writer := multipart.NewWriter(body)
    _ = writer.WriteField("id", "msg123")
    part, _ := writer.CreateFormFile("file", "largefile.txt")
    _, _ = part.Write([]byte("this content is larger than 10 bytes"))
    writer.Close() // This calculates Content-Length

    req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/files/", body)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    req.Header.Set("Content-Type", writer.FormDataContentType())
     // Explicitly set Content-Length if httptest doesn't do it automatically based on body size
     // req.ContentLength = int64(body.Len()) // Usually handled by NewRequest or test server

    recorder := httptest.NewRecorder()

    // Act
    largeFileReceive(recorder, req)

    // Assert
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge, recorder.Code)
    assert.Contains(t, recorder.Body.String(), "Request entity too large") // Specific error message
}

    _ = writer.WriteField("id", "msg123")

    require.NoError(t, err)

func TestLargeFileReceive_AuthChallenge_121(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    _, _, _ = setupTestEnvironment(t)
    challengeBytes := []byte("upload-challenge")
    // Override default mock for authHttpRequest
    authHttpRequest = func(req *http.Request) (types.Uid, []byte, error) {
        return types.ZeroUid, challengeBytes, nil // Return challenge
    }

    // Create a minimal valid multipart body
    body := new(bytes.Buffer)
    writer := multipart.NewWriter(body)
    _ = writer.WriteField("id", "msg456") // Use a different ID
    writer.Close()

    req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/files/", body)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    req.Header.Set("Content-Type", writer.FormDataContentType())
    req.Header.Set("X-Tinode-APIKey", "valid-key")
    recorder := httptest.NewRecorder()

    // Act
    largeFileReceive(recorder, req)

    // Assert
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, recorder.Code) // Challenge uses StatusOK
    resBody := recorder.Body.String()
    assert.Contains(t, resBody, `"code":200`)
    assert.Contains(t, resBody, `"text":"Authentication challenge"`)
    assert.Contains(t, resBody, `"id":"msg456"`) // Check if msgID is included
    encodedChallenge := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(challengeBytes)
    assert.Contains(t, resBody, `"params":{"challenge":"`+encodedChallenge+`"}`)
}

func TestLargeFileReceive_MediaHandlerHeadersStatusPost_671(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    ctrl, mockMediaHandler, _ := setupTestEnvironment(t)
    defer ctrl.Finish()

    // authHttpRequest succeeds by default

    redirectHeaders := http.Header{"X-Redirected": []string{"true"}}
    // Use a status like Accepted or Created, which might indicate async processing
    mockMediaHandler.EXPECT().Headers(gomock.Any(), false).Return(redirectHeaders, http.StatusAccepted, nil)

    // Create minimal body
    body := new(bytes.Buffer)
    writer := multipart.NewWriter(body)
    writer.Close()

    req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/files/", body)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    req.Header.Set("Content-Type", writer.FormDataContentType())
    req.Header.Set("X-Tinode-APIKey", "valid-key")
    recorder := httptest.NewRecorder()

    // Act
    largeFileReceive(recorder, req)

    // Assert
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusAccepted, recorder.Code)
    assert.Equal(t, "true", recorder.Header().Get("X-Redirected"))
    // Body should contain the status message for POST/PUT requests when handler terminates
    assert.Contains(t, recorder.Body.String(), http.StatusText(http.StatusAccepted))
    mockMediaHandler.AssertExpectations(t)
}

    _, mockMediaHandler, _ := setupTestEnvironment(t)
    // authHttpRequest succeeds by default

    // Create a request with invalid multipart data (e.g., incorrect boundary)
    body := bytes.NewBufferString("invalid multipart data")

    require.NoError(t, err)
    // Set a boundary that doesn't match the (non-existent) body structure

    req.Header.Set("X-Tinode-APIKey", "valid-key")
    recorder := httptest.NewRecorder()

    // Act

    // Assert
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusBadRequest, recorder.Code) // ErrMalformed
    assert.Contains(t, recorder.Body.String(), "Malformed request")
    // No expectation on mockMediaHandler.Upload as it shouldn't be reached
}

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
	"github.com/tinode/chat/server/store/types"
)

Test Implementation:
func TestPresParamsPackAcs_VariousInputs_111(t *testing.T) {
    tests := []struct {
        name     string
        params   presParams
        expected *MsgAccessMode
    }{
        {
            name: "Both dWant and dGiven are empty",
            params: presParams{
                dWant:  "",
                dGiven: "",
            },
            expected: nil,
        },
        {
            name: "Only dWant is non-empty",
            params: presParams{
                dWant:  "RW",
                dGiven: "",
            },
            expected: &MsgAccessMode{Want: "RW", Given: ""},
        },
        {
            name: "Only dGiven is non-empty",
            params: presParams{
                dWant:  "",
                dGiven: "R",
            },
            expected: &MsgAccessMode{Want: "", Given: "R"},
        },
        {
            name: "Both dWant and dGiven are non-empty",
            params: presParams{
                dWant:  "RW",
                dGiven: "R",
            },
            expected: &MsgAccessMode{Want: "RW", Given: "R"},
        },
    }

    for _, tt := range tests {
        t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
            result := tt.params.packAcs()
            if tt.expected == nil {
                assert.Nil(t, result)
            } else {
                require.NotNil(t, result)
                assert.Equal(t, tt.expected.Want, result.Want)
                assert.Equal(t, tt.expected.Given, result.Given)
            }
        })
    }
}

import (

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

)

Test Implementation:
func TestTopicAddToPerSubs_VariousScenarios_222(t *testing.T) {
    t.Run("Skip adding self", func(t *testing.T) {
        topic := &Topic{name: "testTopic", perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        topic.addToPerSubs("testTopic", true, true)
        assert.Empty(t, topic.perSubs, "Should not add self to perSubs")
    })

    t.Run("Add non-P2P topic", func(t *testing.T) {
        topic := &Topic{name: "testTopic", perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        topic.addToPerSubs("anotherTopic", true, false)
        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, "anotherTopic")
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: true, enabled: false}, topic.perSubs["anotherTopic"])
    })

    t.Run("Add P2P topic where topic user is uid1", func(t *testing.T) {
        uid1 := types.ParseUserId("usr123")
        uid2 := types.ParseUserId("usr456")
        p2pTopicName := uid1.P2PName(uid2)

        topic := &Topic{name: uid1.UserId(), perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        topic.addToPerSubs(p2pTopicName, true, true)

        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, uid2.UserId(), "Should index P2P topic by the other user's ID")
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: true, enabled: true}, topic.perSubs[uid2.UserId()])
    })

    t.Run("Add P2P topic where topic user is uid2", func(t *testing.T) {
        uid1 := types.ParseUserId("usr123")
        uid2 := types.ParseUserId("usr456")
        p2pTopicName := uid1.P2PName(uid2)

        topic := &Topic{name: uid2.UserId(), perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        topic.addToPerSubs(p2pTopicName, false, false)

        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, uid1.UserId(), "Should index P2P topic by the other user's ID")
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: false, enabled: false}, topic.perSubs[uid1.UserId()])
    })

    t.Run("Add P2P topic with invalid name (should treat as non-P2P)", func(t *testing.T) {
        topic := &Topic{name: "testTopic", perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        invalidP2PName := "invalidP2P"
        topic.addToPerSubs(invalidP2PName, true, true)
        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, invalidP2PName)
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: true, enabled: true}, topic.perSubs[invalidP2PName])
    })
}

Test Implementation:
func TestTopicLoadContacts_SuccessAndError_333(t *testing.T) {
    uid := types.ParseUserId("usr123")

    t.Run("Success case", func(t *testing.T) {
        mockStore := new(storeMocks.UsersPersistenceInterface)
        // Save original and restore after test
        originalStoreUsers := store.Users
        store.Users = mockStore
        defer func() { store.Users = originalStoreUsers }()


        subs := []types.Subscription{
            {
                ObjHeader: types.ObjHeader{Id: "sub1"},
                Topic:     "topic1",
                ModeGiven: types.ModeRead | types.ModePres, // Presencer = true
                ModeWant:  types.ModeRead | types.ModePres,
            },
            {
                 ObjHeader: types.ObjHeader{Id: "sub2"},
                 Topic:     "topic2",
                 ModeGiven: types.ModeRead, // Presencer = false
                 ModeWant:  types.ModeRead | types.ModePres,
            },
            {
                 ObjHeader: types.ObjHeader{Id: "sub3"},
                 Topic:     types.ParseUserId("usr123").P2PName(types.ParseUserId("usr456")), // P2P topic
                 ModeGiven: types.ModeJoin | types.ModePres, // Presencer = true
                 ModeWant:  types.ModeJoin | types.ModePres,
            },
             {
                 ObjHeader: types.ObjHeader{Id: "sub4"},
                 Topic:     "usr123", // Should be skipped
                 ModeGiven: types.ModeJoin | types.ModePres,
                 ModeWant:  types.ModeJoin | types.ModePres,
             },
        }

        mockStore.On("GetSubs", uid).Return(subs, nil)

        topic := &Topic{name: uid.UserId(), perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        err := topic.loadContacts(uid)

        assert.NoError(t, err)
        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, "topic1")
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: false, enabled: true}, topic.perSubs["topic1"])
        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, "topic2")
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: false, enabled: false}, topic.perSubs["topic2"])
        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, "usr456") // P2P topic indexed by other user
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: false, enabled: true}, topic.perSubs["usr456"])
        assert.NotContains(t, topic.perSubs, "usr123", "Should skip self topic") // Ensure self is not added

        mockStore.AssertExpectations(t)
    })

    t.Run("Error case", func(t *testing.T) {
        mockStore := new(storeMocks.UsersPersistenceInterface)
        // Save original and restore after test
        originalStoreUsers := store.Users
        store.Users = mockStore
        defer func() { store.Users = originalStoreUsers }()

        expectedErr := errors.New("database error")
        mockStore.On("GetSubs", uid).Return(nil, expectedErr)

        topic := &Topic{name: uid.UserId(), perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        err := topic.loadContacts(uid)

        assert.Error(t, err)
        assert.Equal(t, expectedErr, err)
        assert.Empty(t, topic.perSubs, "perSubs should be empty on error")

        mockStore.AssertExpectations(t)
    })
}

					require.NotNil(t, reply.Pres)

					assert.Equal(t, tt.expectedReply.Pres.Src, reply.Pres.Src)
					assert.Equal(t, tt.expectedReply.Pres.What, reply.Pres.What)
                    assert.Equal(t, tt.expectedReply.Pres.WantReply, reply.Pres.WantReply)
				default:
					t.Errorf("Expected a reply message, but none was sent")
				}
			} else {
				select {
				case unexpectedReply := <-testHub.routeSrv:
					t.Errorf("Did not expect a reply message, but got one: %+v", unexpectedReply)
				default:
					// Correct, no reply sent
				}
			}
		})

func TestLargeFileServe_OptionsHeadersError_199(t *testing.T) {

    ctrl, mockStoreInstance, mockMediaHandler, _, cleanup := setupTestEnvironment(t)
    defer cleanup()

    store.Store = mockStoreInstance

    expectedError := errors.New("media handler headers error")
    mockStoreInstance.EXPECT().GetMediaHandler().Return(mockMediaHandler)
    mockMediaHandler.EXPECT().Headers(gomock.Any(), true).Return(nil, 0, expectedError)

    // Mock decodeStoreError to return a specific response for this error
    originalDecodeStoreError := decodeStoreError
    decodeStoreError = func(err error, msgId string, ts time.Time, _ time.Time) *ServerComMessage {
        if err == expectedError {
            return &ServerComMessage{Ctrl: &MsgServerCtrl{Code: http.StatusInternalServerError, Text: "Headers Check Failed"}}
        }
        return originalDecodeStoreError(err, msgId, ts, time.Time{})
    }
    defer func() { decodeStoreError = originalDecodeStoreError }()


    req, err := http.NewRequest(http.MethodOptions, "/files/somefile", nil)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    recorder := httptest.NewRecorder()

    // Act
    largeFileServe(recorder, req)

    // Assert
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusInternalServerError, recorder.Code)
    assert.Contains(t, recorder.Body.String(), "Headers Check Failed")
    ctrl.Finish()
}

Test Implementation:
func TestPayloadToData_MsgPayloadWithTrimming_123(t *testing.T) {
	// Arrange
	timestamp := time.Now()
	// Simple plain text content, assuming drafty functions work correctly.
	longContentRunes := make([]rune, push.MaxPayloadLength+10)
	for i := range longContentRunes {
		longContentRunes[i] = 'a'
	}
	longContent := string(longContentRunes)

	// Use a drafty object to ensure Preview can process it
	draftyContent := map[string]interface{}{"txt": longContent}

	payload := &push.Payload{
		What:        push.ActMsg,
		Silent:      false, // Explicitly false initially
		Topic:       "test_topic",
		Timestamp:   timestamp,
		From:        "usr123",
		SeqId:       42,
		ContentType: "text/x-drafty", // Use drafty content type
		Content:     draftyContent,   // Pass the drafty map
		Webrtc:      "started",
		AudioOnly:   true,
		Replace:     "seq123",
	}

	expectedContentTrimmed := string(longContentRunes[:push.MaxPayloadLength]) + "…"
	// Preview function wraps result in JSON string
	expectedPreview, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]interface{}{"txt": expectedContentTrimmed})

	// Act
	data, err := payloadToData(payload)

	// Assert
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, data)
	assert.Equal(t, push.ActMsg, data["what"])
	// Note: Webrtc and Replace make the push silent implicitly (lines 69, 73)
	assert.Equal(t, "true", data["silent"])
	assert.Equal(t, "test_topic", data["topic"])
	assert.Equal(t, timestamp.Format(time.RFC3339Nano), data["ts"])
	assert.Equal(t, "usr123", data["xfrom"])
	assert.Equal(t, "42", data["seq"])
	assert.Equal(t, "text/x-drafty", data["mime"])
	// drafty.PlainText extracts text, drafty.Preview generates rich content preview
	assert.Equal(t, expectedContentTrimmed, data["content"]) // Plain text, trimmed
	assert.JSONEq(t, string(expectedPreview), data["rc"])     // Rich content preview, trimmed, as JSON string
	assert.Equal(t, "started", data["webrtc"])
	assert.Equal(t, "true", data["aonly"])
	assert.Equal(t, "seq123", data["replace"])
}

func TestPayloadToData_ExplicitSilent_911(t *testing.T) {
	// Arrange
	timestamp := time.Now()
	payload := &push.Payload{
		What:      push.ActSub, // Use ActSub which is not implicitly silent
		Silent:    true,        // Explicitly set silent flag
		Topic:     "grp123",
		Timestamp: timestamp,
		From:      "sys",
		ModeWant:  t.ModeCSRead,
		ModeGiven: t.ModeCSRead,
	}

	// Act
	data, err := payloadToData(payload)

	// Assert
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, data)
	assert.Equal(t, push.ActSub, data["what"])
	assert.Equal(t, "true", data["silent"]) // Check if explicit silent flag is set (line 33-35)

func TestPrepareV1Notifications_SkipAndSilenceDevice_202(t *testing.T) {
	// Arrange
	mockDevices := new(storeMocks.DevicesAccessor)
	originalDevices := store.Devices
	store.Devices = mockDevices
	defer func() { store.Devices = originalDevices }()

	uid1 := t.ParseUid("usr111")
	onlineDeviceID := "ios_token_online"
	offlineDeviceID := "ios_token_offline"

	rcpt := &push.Receipt{
		To: map[t.Uid]push.Recipient{
			// Mark user as delivered > 0 and specify the online device
			uid1: {Unread: 5, Delivered: 1, Devices: []string{onlineDeviceID}},
		},
		Payload: push.Payload{
			What:      push.ActMsg,
			Topic:     "grp123",
			Timestamp: time.Now(),
			From:      "usr222",
			SeqId:     1,
			Content:   map[string]interface{}{"txt": "hello"},
		},
	}
	config := &configType{
		TimeToLive:   3600,
		ApnsBundleID: "test.bundle.id",
		Apns:         &common.Config{Enabled: true}, // Enable APNS for alert check
	}

	// Store has two devices, one online (in rcpt.To[uid1].Devices), one offline
	devices := map[t.Uid][]t.DeviceDef{
		uid1: {
			{DeviceId: onlineDeviceID, Platform: "ios"},
			{DeviceId: offlineDeviceID, Platform: "ios"},
		},
	}
	mockDevices.On("GetAll", mock.AnythingOfType("[]types.Uid")).Return(devices, 2, nil).Once()

	// Act
	messages, uids := PrepareV1Notifications(rcpt, config)

	// Assert
	mockDevices.AssertExpectations(t)
	require.Len(t, messages, 1) // Only the offline device should get a push (line 163 skip check)
	require.Len(t, uids, 1)
	assert.Equal(t, uid1, uids[0])

	msg := messages[0]
	assert.Equal(t, offlineDeviceID, msg.Token) // Push sent to offline device
	require.NotNil(t, msg.Apns)
	assert.Nil(t, msg.Android)

	// Check if it was silenced due to Delivered > 0 (line 156-158)
	require.NotNil(t, msg.Data)
	assert.Equal(t, "true", msg.Data["silent"])

	// Verify APNS payload specifics for silent push (like no alert - checked by apnsShouldPresentAlert line 344)
	var payload map[string]interface{}
	err := json.Unmarshal(msg.Apns.Payload, &payload)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	aps, ok := payload["aps"].(map[string]interface{})
	require.True(t, ok)
	_, alertPresent := aps["alert"]
	assert.False(t, alertPresent, "Silent push should not have 'alert' field")
	assert.Equal(t, float64(1), aps["content-available"]) // Should still have content-available (line 336)
	assert.Equal(t, float64(5), aps["badge"])             // Badge should still be sent (line 335)
}

func TestPrepareV1Notifications_P2P_203(t *testing.T) {
	// Arrange
	mockDevices := new(storeMocks.DevicesAccessor)
	originalDevices := store.Devices
	store.Devices = mockDevices
	defer func() { store.Devices = originalDevices }()

	uid1 := t.ParseUid("usr111") // Recipient
	uid2 := t.ParseUid("usr222") // Sender
	p2pTopic := uid1.P2PName(uid2) // Original P2P topic name (e.g., "usr111usr222")

	rcpt := &push.Receipt{
		To: map[t.Uid]push.Recipient{
			uid1: {Unread: 1}, // Recipient is uid1
		},
		Payload: push.Payload{
			What:      push.ActMsg,
			Topic:     p2pTopic,        // Original P2P topic name
			Timestamp: time.Now(),
			From:      uid2.UserId(), // Sender is uid2
			SeqId:     5,
			Content:   map[string]interface{}{"txt": "p2p message"},
		},
	}
	config := &configType{
		ApnsBundleID: "test.bundle.id",
		Apns:         &common.Config{Enabled: true}, // Need APNS enabled for header checks
	}

	devices := map[t.Uid][]t.DeviceDef{
		uid1: {{DeviceId: "p2p_token", Platform: "ios"}},
	}
	mockDevices.On("GetAll", mock.AnythingOfType("[]types.Uid")).Return(devices, 1, nil).Once()

	// Act
	messages, uids := PrepareV1Notifications(rcpt, config)

	// Assert
	mockDevices.AssertExpectations(t)
	require.Len(t, messages, 1)
	require.Len(t, uids, 1)
	assert.Equal(t, uid1, uids[0])

	msg := messages[0]
	assert.Equal(t, "p2p_token", msg.Token)
	require.NotNil(t, msg.Data)
	// Verify the topic name in the data payload is adjusted for the recipient (uid1) (lines 151-153)
	expectedTopicForUid1, err := t.P2PNameForUser(uid1, p2pTopic) // Should be "usr222"
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.Equal(t, expectedTopicForUid1, msg.Data["topic"])
	assert.Equal(t, uid2.UserId(), msg.Data["xfrom"])

	// Verify APNS payload uses the adjusted topic name for thread-id and collapse-id (lines 340, 372)
	require.NotNil(t, msg.Apns)
	require.NotNil(t, msg.Apns.Headers)
	assert.Equal(t, expectedTopicForUid1, msg.Apns.Headers[common.HeaderApnsCollapseID])

	var payloadData map[string]interface{}
	err = json.Unmarshal(msg.Apns.Payload, &payloadData)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	aps, _ := payloadData["aps"].(map[string]interface{})
	require.NotNil(t, aps)
	assert.Equal(t, expectedTopicForUid1, aps["thread-id"])
}

func TestPrepareV1Notifications_Channel_205(t *testing.T) {
	// Arrange
	// No device store mock needed as rcpt.To is empty for channel push (line 114 check)

	channelName := "chn123abc"
	rcpt := &push.Receipt{
		To:      nil, // No individual recipients
		Channel: channelName,
		Payload: push.Payload{
			What:      push.ActMsg,
			Topic:     "grpxyz", // Original topic, used in initial data but replaced for channel push data
			Timestamp: time.Now(),
			From:      "usr789", // Sender info should be removed for channel push
			SeqId:     10,
			Content:   map[string]interface{}{"txt": "channel message"},
		},
	}
	// Config enabling multiple platforms for channel push
	config := &configType{
		TimeToLive:   1800,
		ApnsBundleID: "test.bundle.id",
		Android:      &common.Config{Enabled: true}, // Enable Android
		Apns:         &common.Config{Enabled: true, Payload: common.Payload{Title: "Channel Title"}}, // Enable APNS
		Webpush:      &common.Config{Enabled: true}, // Enable Webpush
	}

	// Act
	messages, uids := PrepareV1Notifications(rcpt, config)

	// Assert
	require.Len(t, messages, 1) // One message for the channel topic (lines 190-208)
	require.Len(t, uids, 1)
	assert.Equal(t, t.ZeroUid, uids[0]) // Placeholder UID for channel push (line 207)

	msg := messages[0]
	assert.Empty(t, msg.Token)           // No token for channel push
	assert.Equal(t, channelName, msg.Topic) // Message topic is the channel name (line 197)
	require.NotNil(t, msg.Data)
	assert.Equal(t, channelName, msg.Data["topic"]) // Data topic is also the channel name (line 193)
	_, fromPresent := msg.Data["xfrom"]
	assert.False(t, fromPresent, "'xfrom' should be removed for channel pushes") // Line 195
	assert.Equal(t, "10", msg.Data["seq"])
	assert.Equal(t, "channel message", msg.Data["content"])

	// Check that payloads for all enabled platforms are present (lines 202, 203, 175-177)
	require.NotNil(t, msg.Android)
	require.NotNil(t, msg.Apns)
	require.NotNil(t, msg.Webpush)
	assert.IsType(t, &fcmv1.WebpushConfig{}, msg.Webpush) // Check webpush config is added

	// Check specific platform details use the channel name
	require.NotNil(t, msg.Android.Notification)
	assert.Equal(t, channelName, msg.Android.Notification.Tag)

	require.NotNil(t, msg.Apns.Headers)
	assert.Equal(t, channelName, msg.Apns.Headers[common.HeaderApnsCollapseID])
	var apsPayload map[string]interface{}
	err := json.Unmarshal(msg.Apns.Payload, &apsPayload)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	aps, _ := apsPayload["aps"].(map[string]interface{})
	require.NotNil(t, aps)
	assert.Equal(t, channelName, aps["thread-id"])
	alert, _ := aps["alert"].(map[string]interface{})
	require.NotNil(t, alert)
	assert.Equal(t, "Channel Title", alert["title"]) // Check title from config
}

Test Implementation:
func TestPrepareV1Notifications_NilConfig_210(t *testing.T) {
	// Arrange
	mockDevices := new(storeMocks.DevicesAccessor)
	originalDevices := store.Devices
	store.Devices = mockDevices
	defer func() { store.Devices = originalDevices }()

	uid1 := t.ParseUid("usr111")
	rcpt := &push.Receipt{
		To: map[t.Uid]push.Recipient{
			uid1: {Unread: 5, Delivered: 0},
		},
		Payload: push.Payload{
			What:      push.ActMsg,
			Topic:     "grp123",
			Timestamp: time.Now(),
			From:      "usr222",
			SeqId:     1,
			Content:   map[string]interface{}{"txt": "hello"},
		},
	}
	// config is nil
	var config *configType = nil // Line 137 handles nil config

	devices := map[t.Uid][]t.DeviceDef{
		uid1: {
			{DeviceId: "android_token_1", Platform: "android"},
			{DeviceId: "ios_token_1", Platform: "ios"},
			{DeviceId: "web_token_1", Platform: "web"},         // Web requires config for Webpush field
			{DeviceId: "unknown_token_1", Platform: "unknown"}, // Handled by default case (line 180)
			{DeviceId: "empty_token_1", Platform: ""},          // Handled by case "" (line 178)
			{DeviceId: "skipped_token", Platform: "android"},   // This one will be skipped later
		},
	}
	// rcpt.To defines uid1, so mock should expect []t.Uid{uid1}
	mockDevices.On("GetAll", mock.AnythingOfType("[]types.Uid")).Return(devices, 6, nil).Once()

	// Act
	// Note: PrepareV1Notifications handles nil config by creating a default one internally (line 139)
	// The platform-specific functions (androidNotificationConfig, etc.) also handle nil config.
	messages, uids := PrepareV1Notifications(rcpt, config)

	// Assert
	mockDevices.AssertExpectations(t)
	// Should generate messages for all devices except the skipped one (if any were specified in skipDevices, none here)
	// and those with empty platform or unknown platform still generate a base message.
	require.Len(t, messages, 6) // One message per device token
	require.Len(t, uids, 6)
	assert.Contains(t, uids, uid1) // All UIDs should be uid1 here

	// Check platforms were handled gracefully with nil config (defaults applied)
	foundPlatforms := map[string]bool{}
	for _, msg := range messages {
		require.NotNil(t, msg.Data) // Data should always be present
		switch msg.Token {
		case "android_token_1":
			foundPlatforms["android"] = true
			require.NotNil(t, msg.Android)
			assert.Nil(t, msg.Android.Notification) // Notification part requires config.Android.Enabled (line 271)
			assert.Equal(t, strconv.Itoa(defaultTimeToLive)+"s", msg.Android.Ttl) // Default TTL (line 243)
		case "ios_token_1":
			foundPlatforms["ios"] = true
			require.NotNil(t, msg.Apns)
			require.NotNil(t, msg.Apns.Headers)
			require.NotEmpty(t, msg.Apns.Payload) // Basic APS payload is always generated
			var payload map[string]interface{}
			err := json.Unmarshal(msg.Apns.Payload, &payload)
			require.NoError(t, err)
			aps, ok := payload["aps"].(map[string]interface{})
			require.True(t, ok)
			_, alertPresent := aps["alert"]
			// Alert should not be present because apnsShouldPresentAlert returns false with nil config (line 305)
			assert.False(t, alertPresent, "Alert should not be present with nil config")
			assert.Equal(t, strconv.Itoa(defaultTimeToLive), msg.Apns.Headers[common.HeaderApnsExpiration][:10]) // Check default expiration
		case "web_token_1":
			foundPlatforms["web"] = true
			// Webpush field is only added if config != nil && config.Webpush != nil && config.Webpush.Enabled (line 175)
			assert.Nil(t, msg.Webpush)
		case "unknown_token_1": // Should have base message, no platform specifics (line 181 logs warning)
			foundPlatforms["unknown"] = true
			assert.Nil(t, msg.Android)
			assert.Nil(t, msg.Apns)
			assert.Nil(t, msg.Webpush)
		case "empty_token_1": // Should have base message, no platform specifics (line 179 ignore)
			foundPlatforms["empty"] = true
			assert.Nil(t, msg.Android)
			assert.Nil(t, msg.Apns)
			assert.Nil(t, msg.Webpush)
		case "skipped_token":
			foundPlatforms["skipped"] = true // Should still be processed here as skipDevices is empty
			require.NotNil(t, msg.Android) // Basic android config generated
		default:
			t.Errorf("Unexpected message token: %s", msg.Token)
		}
	}
	assert.True(t, foundPlatforms["android"])
	assert.True(t, foundPlatforms["ios"])
	assert.True(t, foundPlatforms["web"])
	assert.True(t, foundPlatforms["unknown"])
	assert.True(t, foundPlatforms["empty"])
	assert.True(t, foundPlatforms["skipped"])
}

func TestApnsShouldPresentAlert_Various_601(t *testing.T) {

	configDisabled := &configType{Apns: &common.Config{Enabled: false}}

		name       string
		what       string
		callStatus string // data["webrtc"]
		isSilent   string // data["silent"]
		config     *configType
		expected   bool
	}{
		// config != nil && config.Apns != nil && config.Apns.Enabled && what != push.ActRead && callStatus == "" && isSilent == ""
		{"Enabled Msg", push.ActMsg, "", "", configEnabled, true},
		{"Enabled Sub", push.ActSub, "", "", configEnabled, true},
		{"Enabled Read", push.ActRead, "", "", configEnabled, false},   // what == push.ActRead
		{"Enabled Call", push.ActMsg, "started", "", configEnabled, false}, // callStatus != ""
		{"Enabled Silent", push.ActMsg, "", "true", configEnabled, false}, // isSilent != ""
		{"Disabled Msg", push.ActMsg, "", "", configDisabled, false},   // config.Apns.Enabled == false
		{"Nil APNS Config Msg", push.ActMsg, "", "", configNilApns, false}, // config.Apns == nil
		{"Nil Config Msg", push.ActMsg, "", "", configNil, false},       // config == nil
	}

			actual := apnsShouldPresentAlert(tc.what, tc.callStatus, tc.isSilent, tc.config) // Line 305

		})
	}

func TestApnsNotificationConfig_Read_702(t *testing.T) {
	// Arrange
	what := push.ActRead // Line 328 triggers specific logic
	topic := "usr123"
	data := map[string]string{}
	unread := 0 // Read receipts don't usually affect badge
	bundleId := "com.example.read"
	config := &configType{
		TimeToLive:   0, // Use default TTL
		ApnsBundleID: bundleId,
		Apns:         &common.Config{Enabled: true}, // Enabled, but Read shouldn't alert (line 305 check)
	}

	// Act
	ac := apnsNotificationConfig(what, topic, data, unread, config)

	// Assert
	require.NotNil(t, ac)
	require.NotNil(t, ac.Headers)
	require.NotNil(t, ac.Payload)

	// Check Headers
	assert.Equal(t, bundleId, ac.Headers[common.HeaderApnsTopic])
	assert.Equal(t, topic, ac.Headers[common.HeaderApnsCollapseID])
	assert.Equal(t, "5", ac.Headers[common.HeaderApnsPriority])                                // Low priority (line 329)
	assert.Equal(t, string(common.ApnsPushTypeBackground), ac.Headers[common.HeaderApnsPushType]) // Background push type (line 331)
	// Check default expiration (line 310)
	expiresStr := ac.Headers[common.HeaderApnsExpiration]
	expiresUnix, err := strconv.ParseInt(expiresStr, 10, 64)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	expectedExpires := time.Now().UTC().Add(defaultTimeToLive * time.Second).Unix()
	assert.InDelta(t, expectedExpires, expiresUnix, 5)

	// Check Payload
	var payload map[string]interface{}
	err = json.Unmarshal(ac.Payload, &payload)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	aps, ok := payload["aps"].(map[string]interface{})
	require.True(t, ok)
	assert.Equal(t, float64(unread), aps["badge"])
	assert.Equal(t, float64(1), aps["content-available"]) // Still has content-available (line 336)
	assert.Equal(t, string(common.InterruptionLevelPassive), aps["interruption-level"]) // Passive interruption (line 330)
	_, alertPresent := aps["alert"]
	assert.False(t, alertPresent, "Alert should not be present for ActRead") // Checked by apnsShouldPresentAlert (line 344)
}

func TestSendMessageLp_QueueLimitExceeded_101(t *testing.T) {
    _, _ = setupGlobals(t)

    // Simulate the condition len(sess.send) > sendQueueLimit
    // Create a session where the length of the send channel buffer is greater than sendQueueLimit.
    // Note: This assumes sendQueueLimit is accessible or can be reasonably simulated.
    // Here, we use the package-level const sendQueueLimit directly.
    sess := &Session{
        sid:  "test-sid-limit",
        send: make(chan any, sendQueueLimit+1), // Capacity > limit
    }
    // Fill the channel to ensure len > sendQueueLimit
    for i := 0; i < sendQueueLimit+1; i++ {
        // Use non-blocking send; if the channel were full, this would panic.
        // This setup relies on the channel having capacity > sendQueueLimit.
         select {
         case sess.send <- i:
         default:
             t.Fatalf("Failed to fill channel for test setup")
         }
    }

    // Verify test setup: len(sess.send) should now be sendQueueLimit + 1
    require.Greater(t, len(sess.send), sendQueueLimit, "Test setup failed: len(send) should be > sendQueueLimit")

    wrt := httptest.NewRecorder()

    // Act
    result := sess.sendMessageLp(wrt, "new message")

    // Assert
    assert.False(t, result, "sendMessageLp should return false when queue limit exceeded")
    // Optionally check logs if a logger mock is set up
}

func TestReadOnce_RequestTooLarge_110(t *testing.T) {
    g, _ := setupGlobals(t)
    g.maxMessageSize = 10 // Set a small limit

    sess := newTestSession("test-sid-toolarge")
    wrt := httptest.NewRecorder()
    // Create a request with ContentLength > maxMessageSize
    bodyContent := "this body is much too long for the limit"
    req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/", strings.NewReader(bodyContent))
    // Set ContentLength explicitly, as httptest might set it automatically based on reader.
    // We need ContentLength to be checked *before* reading the body via MaxBytesReader.
    req.ContentLength = int64(len(bodyContent)) // 42
    require.Greater(t, req.ContentLength, g.maxMessageSize, "ContentLength should be > maxMessageSize for this test")

    // Act
    code, err := sess.readOnce(wrt, req)

    // Assert
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge, code, "Status code should indicate entity too large")
    assert.Error(t, err)
    // The error message comes from the stdlib http.MaxBytesReader or our check
    // Let's check for the specific error we return
    assert.EqualError(t, err, "request too large")
}

    sess := &MockSession{Session: *newTestSession("test-sid-commsg")}
    wrt := httptest.NewRecorder()
    req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/", nil)

    msgToSend := &ServerComMessage{Id: "msg1", Ctrl: &MsgServerCtrl{Code: 200, Text: "OK"}}
    // This is the expected serialized form based on the message structure
    serializedMsg := []byte(`{"ctrl":{"id":"msg1","code":200,"text":"OK","ts":"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"}}`) // Adjust ts if needed

    // Mock the serializeAndUpdateStats call
    sess.Mock.On("serializeAndUpdateStats", msgToSend).Return(serializedMsg).Once()

    // Use a context to prevent the test from hanging if writeOnce doesn't exit
    ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(req.Context(), 100*time.Millisecond)
    defer cancel()
    req = req.WithContext(ctx)

    // Send the message in a separate goroutine
    go func() {
        // Ensure channel has buffer or receiver is ready
        time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond) // Small delay
        select {
        case sess.send <- msgToSend:
        case <-ctx.Done():
             t.Log("Context cancelled before sending message")
        }
    }()

    // Act
    sess.writeOnce(wrt, req) // This should read the message, serialize, send, and return

    // Assert
    sess.Mock.AssertCalled(t, "serializeAndUpdateStats", msgToSend)
    assert.Equal(t, string(serializedMsg), wrt.Body.String())
}

func TestServeLongPoll_ValidAPIKey_Headers_127(t *testing.T) {
    g, mockStore := setupServeLongPollTest(t)
    g.tlsStrictMaxAge = "63072000" // Set a specific HSTS value

    // --- Test with HTTP/1.1 ---
    wrt11 := httptest.NewRecorder()
    req11 := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/lp?apikey=test-api-key&sid=nonexistentsid", nil)
    req11.ProtoMajor = 1
    req11.ProtoMinor = 1
    mockStore.On("Get", "nonexistentsid").Return(nil).Once() // Ensure session lookup fails to stop processing

    serveLongPoll(wrt11, req11)

    assert.Equal(t, "text/plain", wrt11.Header().Get("Content-Type"), "HTTP/1.1 Content-Type")
    assert.Equal(t, "max-age63072000", wrt11.Header().Get("Strict-Transport-Security"), "HTTP/1.1 HSTS")
    assert.Equal(t, "*", wrt11.Header().Get("Access-Control-Allow-Origin"), "HTTP/1.1 CORS")
    assert.Equal(t, "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate", wrt11.Header().Get("Cache-Control"), "HTTP/1.1 Cache-Control")
    assert.Equal(t, "0", wrt11.Header().Get("Expires"), "HTTP/1.1 Expires")
    assert.Empty(t, wrt11.Header().Get("Pragma"), "HTTP/1.1 Pragma should be empty")
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusForbidden, wrt11.Code) // Because session lookup failed
    mockStore.AssertExpectations(t) // Ensure mock was called


    // --- Test with HTTP/1.0 ---
     // Need a new mock store instance for the second call
    g, mockStore2 := setupServeLongPollTest(t)
    g.tlsStrictMaxAge = "63072000"
    wrt10 := httptest.NewRecorder()
    req10 := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/lp?apikey=test-api-key&sid=nonexistentsid2", nil)
    req10.ProtoMajor = 1
    req10.ProtoMinor = 0
    mockStore2.On("Get", "nonexistentsid2").Return(nil).Once() // Ensure session lookup fails

    serveLongPoll(wrt10, req10)

    assert.Equal(t, "text/plain", wrt10.Header().Get("Content-Type"), "HTTP/1.0 Content-Type")
    assert.Equal(t, "no-cache", wrt10.Header().Get("Pragma"), "HTTP/1.0 Pragma")
    assert.Empty(t, wrt10.Header().Get("Cache-Control"), "HTTP/1.0 Cache-Control should be empty")
    assert.Equal(t, "0", wrt10.Header().Get("Expires"), "HTTP/1.0 Expires")
     assert.Equal(t, http.StatusForbidden, wrt10.Code) // Because session lookup failed
    mockStore2.AssertExpectations(t) // Ensure mock was called
}

Test Implementation:
func TestServeLongPoll_NewSession_128(t *testing.T) {
    g, mockStore := setupServeLongPollTest(t)

    wrt := httptest.NewRecorder()
    // Request without 'sid' parameter, with API key and client ID 'id'
    req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodPost, "/lp?apikey=test-api-key&id=clientReqId123", nil)
    req.RemoteAddr = "1.2.3.4:5678"

    newSid := "newSessionIDGenerated"
    // Create a session structure to be returned by the mock
    createdSession := newTestSession(newSid)
    // Mock NewSession to return the created session and count 1
    mockStore.On("NewSession", wrt, "").Return(&createdSession.Session, 1).Once()

    serveLongPoll(wrt, req)

    // Assertions
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, wrt.Code, "Should return 201 Created")
    // Verify NewSession was called correctly
    mockStore.AssertCalled(t, "NewSession", wrt, "")
    // Check if remote address was assigned to the session
    assert.Equal(t, "1.2.3.4:5678", createdSession.remoteAddr)

    // Verify the response body structure
    var respPkt ServerComMessage
    err := json.Unmarshal(wrt.Body.Bytes(), &respPkt)
    require.NoError(t, err, "Failed to unmarshal response body")
    require.NotNil(t, respPkt.Ctrl, "Response should have a Ctrl message")
    assert.Equal(t, 201, respPkt.Ctrl.Code, "Ctrl code should be 201")
    assert.Equal(t, "Created", respPkt.Ctrl.Text, "Ctrl text should be 'Created'")
    assert.Equal(t, "clientReqId123", respPkt.Ctrl.Id, "Ctrl ID should match request ID")
    require.NotNil(t, respPkt.Ctrl.Params, "Ctrl params should not be nil")
    // Params are returned as map[string]interface{} after json unmarshal
    paramsMap, ok := respPkt.Ctrl.Params.(map[string]any)
    require.True(t, ok, "Params should be a map[string]any")
    assert.Equal(t, newSid, paramsMap["sid"], "Params should contain the new session ID")
}

func TestServeLongPoll_ExistingSession_AddrChange_130(t *testing.T) {

    sid := "existingSIDAddrChange"

    existingSession.remoteAddr = "1.1.1.1:1111" // Initial remote address
    mockStore.On("Get", sid).Return(&existingSession.Session).Once()

    wrt := httptest.NewRecorder()
    req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/lp?apikey=test-api-key&sid="+sid, nil)
    req.RemoteAddr = "2.2.2.2:2222" // New remote address

    ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(req.Context(), 50*time.Millisecond)

    serveLongPoll(wrt, req) // Should find session, update addr, then call writeOnce (which times out/cancels)

    mockStore.AssertCalled(t, "Get", sid)
    assert.Equal(t, "2.2.2.2:2222", existingSession.remoteAddr, "Session remote address should be updated")
    // Log check would be ideal: logs.Warn.Println("longPoll: remote address changed", sid, addr)
}

Test Implementation:
func TestServeLongPoll_ExistingSession_NoPayload_WriteOnce_134(t *testing.T) {
    g, mockStore := setupServeLongPollTest(t)

    sid := "existingSIDNoPayloadWrite"
    sess := newTestSession(sid)
    mockStore.On("Get", sid).Return(&sess.Session).Once()

    wrt := httptest.NewRecorder()
    // Request with no body, ContentLength will be 0
    req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/lp?apikey=test-api-key&sid="+sid, nil)
    require.EqualValues(t, 0, req.ContentLength, "Request ContentLength should be 0")

    // writeOnce will be called. Prevent it from hanging using context cancellation.
    ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(req.Context(), 50*time.Millisecond)
    defer cancel()
    req = req.WithContext(ctx)

    serveLongPoll(wrt, req)

    mockStore.AssertCalled(t, "Get", sid)
    // Asserting writeOnce was called is tricky. We check the status code.
    // If writeOnce timed out or context cancelled without error, status should be OK.
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, wrt.Code)
    // The body might be empty if context cancelled before writeOnce sent anything.
    // Or it could be the empty timeout packet "".
    assert.Condition(t, func() bool { return wrt.Body.String() == "" }, "Body should be empty")
}

import (

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

Test Implementation:
func TestTopicAddToPerSubs_VariousScenarios_222(t *testing.T) {
    t.Run("Skip adding self", func(t *testing.T) {
        topic := &Topic{name: "testTopic", perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        topic.addToPerSubs("testTopic", true, true)
        assert.Empty(t, topic.perSubs, "Should not add self to perSubs")
    })

    t.Run("Add non-P2P topic", func(t *testing.T) {
        topic := &Topic{name: "testTopic", perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        topic.addToPerSubs("anotherTopic", true, false)
        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, "anotherTopic")
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: true, enabled: false}, topic.perSubs["anotherTopic"])
    })

    t.Run("Add P2P topic where topic user is uid1", func(t *testing.T) {
        uid1 := types.ParseUserId("usr123")
        uid2 := types.ParseUserId("usr456")
        p2pTopicName := uid1.P2PName(uid2)

        topic := &Topic{name: uid1.UserId(), perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        topic.addToPerSubs(p2pTopicName, true, true)

        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, uid2.UserId(), "Should index P2P topic by the other user's ID")
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: true, enabled: true}, topic.perSubs[uid2.UserId()])
    })

    t.Run("Add P2P topic where topic user is uid2", func(t *testing.T) {
        uid1 := types.ParseUserId("usr123")
        uid2 := types.ParseUserId("usr456")
        p2pTopicName := uid1.P2PName(uid2)

        topic := &Topic{name: uid2.UserId(), perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        topic.addToPerSubs(p2pTopicName, false, false)

        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, uid1.UserId(), "Should index P2P topic by the other user's ID")
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: false, enabled: false}, topic.perSubs[uid1.UserId()])
    })

    t.Run("Add P2P topic with invalid name (should treat as non-P2P)", func(t *testing.T) {
        topic := &Topic{name: "testTopic", perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        invalidP2PName := "invalidP2P" // This won't parse correctly with types.ParseP2P
        topic.addToPerSubs(invalidP2PName, true, true)
        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, invalidP2PName)
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: true, enabled: true}, topic.perSubs[invalidP2PName])
    })
}

Test Implementation:
func TestTopicLoadContacts_SuccessAndError_333(t *testing.T) {
    uid := types.ParseUserId("usr123")

    t.Run("Success case", func(t *testing.T) {
        mockCtrl := gomock.NewController(t)
        defer mockCtrl.Finish()
        mockStore := storeMocks.NewMockUsersPersistenceInterface(mockCtrl)

        // Save original and restore after test
        originalStoreUsers := store.Users
        store.Users = mockStore
        defer func() { store.Users = originalStoreUsers }()

        subs := []types.Subscription{
            {
                ObjHeader: types.ObjHeader{Id: "sub1"},
                Topic:     "topic1",
                ModeGiven: types.ModeRead | types.ModePres, // Presencer = true
                ModeWant:  types.ModeRead | types.ModePres,
            },
            {
                 ObjHeader: types.ObjHeader{Id: "sub2"},
                 Topic:     "topic2",
                 ModeGiven: types.ModeRead, // Presencer = false
                 ModeWant:  types.ModeRead | types.ModePres,
            },
            {
                 ObjHeader: types.ObjHeader{Id: "sub3"},
                 Topic:     types.ParseUserId("usr123").P2PName(types.ParseUserId("usr456")), // P2P topic
                 ModeGiven: types.ModeJoin | types.ModePres, // Presencer = true
                 ModeWant:  types.ModeJoin | types.ModePres,
            },
             {
                 ObjHeader: types.ObjHeader{Id: "sub4"},
                 Topic:     "usr123", // Should be skipped
                 ModeGiven: types.ModeJoin | types.ModePres,
                 ModeWant:  types.ModeJoin | types.ModePres,
             },
        }

        mockStore.EXPECT().GetSubs(uid).Return(subs, nil)

        topic := &Topic{name: uid.UserId(), perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        err := topic.loadContacts(uid)

        assert.NoError(t, err)
        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, "topic1")
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: false, enabled: true}, topic.perSubs["topic1"])
        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, "topic2")
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: false, enabled: false}, topic.perSubs["topic2"])
        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, "usr456") // P2P topic indexed by other user
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: false, enabled: true}, topic.perSubs["usr456"])
        assert.NotContains(t, topic.perSubs, "usr123", "Should skip self topic") // Ensure self is not added

    })

    t.Run("Error case", func(t *testing.T) {
         mockCtrl := gomock.NewController(t)
        defer mockCtrl.Finish()
        mockStore := storeMocks.NewMockUsersPersistenceInterface(mockCtrl)

        // Save original and restore after test
        originalStoreUsers := store.Users
        store.Users = mockStore
        defer func() { store.Users = originalStoreUsers }()


        expectedErr := errors.New("database error")
        mockStore.EXPECT().GetSubs(uid).Return(nil, expectedErr)

        topic := &Topic{name: uid.UserId(), perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        err := topic.loadContacts(uid)

        assert.Error(t, err)
        assert.Equal(t, expectedErr, err)
        assert.Empty(t, topic.perSubs, "perSubs should be empty on error")

    })
}

// Helper to reset expvar state between tests
func resetExpvar(vars ...string) {
    // Expvar doesn't have an UnpublishAll or similar.
    // This is fragile. Best practice is often running tests in separate processes or using unique names.
    // We nil out known vars.
    knownVars := []string{"Uptime", "NumGoroutines", "DbStats"}
    knownVars = append(knownVars, vars...)
    for _, name := range knownVars {
        if v := expvar.Get(name); v != nil {
            // Attempt to set to nil, though expvar might prevent this or it might not fully clean up.
            // Re-publishing with nil is the documented way to effectively remove simple types.
            expvar.Publish(name, nil)
        }
    }
    // Re-register mandatory ones if needed, but generally avoid global state manipulation.
}

// TestMain for setup/teardown
func TestMain(m *testing.M) {
    // Disable logs during testing
    logs.Init(ioutil.Discard, "")

    // Run tests
    exitCode := m.Run()

    // Cleanup: Ensure statsUpdater goroutine doesn't linger if a test fails badly
    if globals.statsUpdate != nil {
        // Try to shut it down gracefully
        select {
        case globals.statsUpdate <- nil:
        case <-time.After(50 * time.Millisecond):
            // Goroutine might be stuck, log or handle error
        }
    }
     resetExpvar() // Final cleanup

    os.Exit(exitCode)
}

Test Implementation:
func TestHistogramAddSample_BelowFirstBound_123(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    bounds := []float64{10.0, 20.0, 30.0}
    h := &histogram{
        CountPerBucket: make([]int64, len(bounds)+1),
        Bounds:         bounds,
    }
    value := 5.0

    // Act
    h.addSample(value)

    // Assert
    assert.Equal(t, int64(1), h.Count)
    assert.Equal(t, value, h.Sum)
    // Value 5.0 is less than bounds[0] (10.0), so it should go into bucket 0.
    assert.Equal(t, int64(1), h.CountPerBucket[0])
    assert.Equal(t, int64(0), h.CountPerBucket[1])
    assert.Equal(t, int64(0), h.CountPerBucket[2])
    assert.Equal(t, int64(0), h.CountPerBucket[3])
    assert.Equal(t, []int64{1, 0, 0, 0}, h.CountPerBucket) // Verify entire slice
}

func TestStatsInit_EmptyPath_112(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    mux := http.NewServeMux()
    path := ""
    originalStatsUpdate := globals.statsUpdate // Save original state
    globals.statsUpdate = nil                 // Ensure it's nil initially
    resetExpvar()                             // Clear expvar state

    // Act
    statsInit(mux, path, time.Now) // Pass time.Now for the new signature

    // Assert

    globals.statsUpdate = originalStatsUpdate

Test Implementation:
func TestStatsInit_ValidPath_114(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    mux := http.NewServeMux()
    path := "/teststats"
    originalStatsUpdate := globals.statsUpdate // Save original state
    globals.statsUpdate = nil                 // Ensure it's nil initially
    resetExpvar()                             // Clear expvar state

    // Act
    statsInit(mux, path, time.Now) // Pass time.Now for the new signature

    // Ensure cleanup happens even on failure
    defer func() {
        if globals.statsUpdate != nil {
            globals.statsUpdate <- nil // Signal shutdown
            time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond) // Allow time for shutdown
        }
         resetExpvar() // Clean up published vars
        globals.statsUpdate = originalStatsUpdate // Restore original channel state
    }()


    // Assert
    require.NotNil(t, globals.statsUpdate, "globals.statsUpdate should be initialized")
    assert.Equal(t, 1024, cap(globals.statsUpdate), "globals.statsUpdate should have capacity 1024")

    // Check if the handler is registered by trying to serve a request
    req, err := http.NewRequest("GET", path, nil)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    recorder := httptest.NewRecorder()
    mux.ServeHTTP(recorder, req)
    // We expect expvar handler to return OK and some JSON content
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, recorder.Code)
    assert.Contains(t, recorder.Body.String(), "Uptime") // Check for expected content

    // Check if default expvars are published
    uptimeVar := expvar.Get("Uptime")
    require.NotNil(t, uptimeVar)
    _, ok := uptimeVar.(expvar.Func) // Check type
    assert.True(t, ok)

    goroutineVar := expvar.Get("NumGoroutines")
    require.NotNil(t, goroutineVar)
    _, ok = goroutineVar.(expvar.Func) // Check type
    assert.True(t, ok)

    // Check values (Goroutines > 0, Uptime >= 0)
    assert.True(t, goroutineVar.(expvar.Func)().(int) > 0)
    // Allow for slight negative due to timing, check >= -0.1
    assert.True(t, uptimeVar.(expvar.Func)().(float64) >= -0.1)
}

Test Implementation:
func TestStatsRegisterDbStats_ValidFunc_116(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    ctrl := gomock.NewController(t)
    defer ctrl.Finish()

    mockStore := storeMocks.NewMockPersistentStorageInterface(ctrl) // Use corrected mock
    originalStore := store.Store // Backup original store
    store.Store = mockStore      // Inject mock
    defer func() {
        store.Store = originalStore // Restore original store
        resetExpvar("DbStats") // Clean up published var
    }()

    expectedData := map[string]int{"connections": 10, "queries": 100}
    dbStatsFunc := func() interface{} {
        return expectedData
    }
    mockStore.EXPECT().DbStats().Return(dbStatsFunc) // Expect call, return valid func

    resetExpvar("DbStats") // Clear previous DbStats if any

    // Act
    statsRegisterDbStats()

    // Assert
    ev := expvar.Get("DbStats")
    require.NotNil(t, ev, "DbStats should be published")
    require.IsType(t, expvar.Func(nil), ev, "DbStats should be of type expvar.Func")

    // Verify the function returns the expected data
    f := ev.(expvar.Func)
    data := f()
    assert.Equal(t, expectedData, data)

    // Verify the string representation (JSON)
    expectedJSON := `{"connections":10,"queries":100}`
    assert.JSONEq(t, expectedJSON, ev.String())
}

func TestStatsRegisterHistogram_Success_118(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    name := "TestHistVarRegSuccess"
    bounds := []float64{1.5, 2.5, 3.5}
    resetExpvar(name) // Ensure clean state

    // Act
    statsRegisterHistogram(name, bounds)

    // Assert
    ev := expvar.Get(name)
    require.NotNil(t, ev, "Variable should be registered")

    hist, ok := ev.(*histogram)
    require.True(t, ok, "Variable should be of type *histogram")
    assert.Equal(t, bounds, hist.Bounds, "Bounds should match")
    expectedBucketCount := len(bounds) + 1
    require.Len(t, hist.CountPerBucket, expectedBucketCount, "Bucket count should be len(bounds)+1")
    // Check buckets are initialized to zero
    for _, count := range hist.CountPerBucket {
        assert.Equal(t, int64(0), count)
    }
    assert.Equal(t, int64(0), hist.Count)
    assert.Equal(t, 0.0, hist.Sum)

    // Cleanup
    resetExpvar(name)
}

func TestStatsSet_FullChannel_121(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    originalStatsUpdate := globals.statsUpdate
    // Use a buffered channel of size 1 and fill it
    globals.statsUpdate = make(chan *varUpdate, 1)
    globals.statsUpdate <- &varUpdate{varname: "dummy", value: int64(1)} // Fill the channel
    defer func() { globals.statsUpdate = originalStatsUpdate }() // Cleanup

    name := "TestSetVarFullChan"
    val := int64(101)

    // Act & Assert: Should not block indefinitely
    done := make(chan bool)
    go func() {
        statsSet(name, val)
        close(done)
    }()

    select {
    case <-done:
        // Test passed, function returned without blocking
    case <-time.After(50 * time.Millisecond): // Increased timeout
        t.Fatal("statsSet blocked unexpectedly on full channel")
    }

    // Ensure the original dummy update is still the only one in the channel
    require.Len(t, globals.statsUpdate, 1, "Channel should still contain the initial dummy update")
    upd := <-globals.statsUpdate
    assert.Equal(t, "dummy", upd.varname) // Verify it's the dummy one
}

Test Implementation:
func TestStatsUpdater_AllOperations_130(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    originalStatsUpdate := globals.statsUpdate
    globals.statsUpdate = make(chan *varUpdate, 10) // Buffered channel for updates
    defer func() { globals.statsUpdate = originalStatsUpdate }()

    // Register variables for testing
    intVarName := "UpdaterIntVarTest"
    histVarName := "UpdaterHistVarTest"
    bounds := []float64{5.0, 15.0}
    resetExpvar(intVarName, histVarName) // Clear previous state
    statsRegisterInt(intVarName)
    statsRegisterHistogram(histVarName, bounds)

    // Start the updater in a goroutine
    updaterDone := make(chan bool)
    go func() {
        statsUpdater()
        close(updaterDone)
    }()

    // Send updates via the channel directly to simulate statsSet/Inc/AddHistSample
    globals.statsUpdate <- &varUpdate{varname: intVarName, value: int64(100), inc: false} // Set
    globals.statsUpdate <- &varUpdate{varname: intVarName, value: int64(50), inc: true} // Inc
    globals.statsUpdate <- &varUpdate{varname: intVarName, value: int64(-25), inc: true} // Dec
    globals.statsUpdate <- &varUpdate{varname: histVarName, value: 3.0} // Hist sample
    globals.statsUpdate <- &varUpdate{varname: histVarName, value: 7.0} // Hist sample
    globals.statsUpdate <- &varUpdate{varname: histVarName, value: 20.0} // Hist sample

    // Send shutdown signal directly
    globals.statsUpdate <- nil

    // Wait for updater to finish
    select {
    case <-updaterDone:
        // Updater finished cleanly
    case <-time.After(100 * time.Millisecond): // Increased timeout
        t.Fatal("statsUpdater did not shut down")
    }

    // Assert Int variable state
    intEv := expvar.Get(intVarName)
    require.NotNil(t, intEv)
    intVar, ok := intEv.(*expvar.Int)
    require.True(t, ok)
    assert.Equal(t, int64(125), intVar.Value(), "Int value mismatch (100 + 50 - 25)") // 100 + 50 - 25 = 125

    // Assert Histogram variable state
    histEv := expvar.Get(histVarName)
    require.NotNil(t, histEv)
    histVar, ok := histEv.(*histogram)
    require.True(t, ok)
    assert.Equal(t, int64(3), histVar.Count, "Histogram count mismatch")
    assert.InDelta(t, 3.0+7.0+20.0, histVar.Sum, 0.001, "Histogram sum mismatch") // Use InDelta for float comparison
    // Buckets: (-inf, 5.0), [5.0, 15.0), [15.0, +inf)
    // Samples: 3.0 (bucket 0), 7.0 (bucket 1), 20.0 (bucket 2)
    assert.Equal(t, []int64{1, 1, 1}, histVar.CountPerBucket, "Histogram buckets mismatch")

    // Assert channel is now nil (due to shutdown logic in statsUpdater)
    assert.Nil(t, globals.statsUpdate, "globals.statsUpdate should be nil after shutdown")

    // Cleanup expvars (redundant due to resetExpvar at start/defer, but safe)
    resetExpvar(intVarName, histVarName)
}

func TestMessageLoop_NodeNilInLoop_925(t *testing.T) {
	// Arrange
	mockStream := new(pbxMocks.Node_MessageLoopServer)
	mockSessStore := new(mockSessionStore)
	globals = Globals{
		sessionStore: mockSessStore,
	}

	sess := newTestSession(mockStream)

	mockSessStore.On("NewSession", mockStream, "").Return(sess, 1)
    mockSessStore.On("Delete", sess).Return() // Expect cleanup


	p := &peer.Peer{Addr: &net.TCPAddr{IP: net.ParseIP("127.0.0.1"), Port: 12345}}
	ctx := peer.NewContext(context.Background(), p)
	mockStream.On("Context").Return(ctx)

    // Mock stream Send (needed by writeGrpcLoop potentially triggered via dispatch)
    mockStream.On("Send", mock.AnythingOfType("*pbx.ServerMsg")).Return(nil).Maybe()

	// Mock stream Recv: first a valid message, then another one that triggers the close
    clientMsg1 := &pbx.ClientMsg{Message: &pbx.ClientMsg_Hi{Hi: &pbx.ClientHi{Id: "1"}}}
    // Use a special message ID that our mocked dispatch will recognize
    clientMsgClose := &pbx.ClientMsg{Message: &pbx.ClientMsg_Hi{Hi: &pbx.ClientHi{Id: "closeme"}}}
    mockStream.On("Recv").Return(clientMsg1, nil).Once()
    mockStream.On("Recv").Return(clientMsgClose, nil).Once()
	// After the second message, Recv won't be called again as the loop breaks

	// Act
	grpcServer := &grpcNodeServer{}
	err := grpcServer.MessageLoop(mockStream) // This will run the loop

    // Ensure background loops are stopped
    // Note: The loop should break *before* stop is closed in this scenario
    // But we close it anyway for consistency in cleanup
    close(sess.stop)
	time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond)

    originalLimit := sendQueueLimit
    sendQueueLimit = testQueueLimit // Temporarily override global limit
    defer func() { sendQueueLimit = originalLimit }() // Restore original limit

    mockStream := new(pbxMocks.Node_MessageLoopServer)
    // Create session with the test limit size channel
    sess := &Session{
        sid:        "test-queue-limit",
        proto:      GRPC,
        send:       make(chan any, testQueueLimit), // Use the test limit
        stop:       make(chan any, 1),

        bkgTimer:   time.NewTimer(1 * time.Hour),
        lock:       sync.Mutex{},
        grpcnode:   mockStream,
    }

    // Fill the queue
    for i := 0; i < testQueueLimit; i++ {
        // Use non-blocking send to fill the buffer quickly
        select {
        case sess.send <- &pbx.ServerMsg{}:
        default:
            t.Fatalf("Failed to fill send queue buffer")
        }
    }
    // Ensure the queue is actually full
    require.Len(t, sess.send, testQueueLimit, "Send queue should be full")


    // Act

    // Assert
    assert.False(t, result, "sendMessageGrpc should return false when queue limit is exceeded")
    mockStream.AssertNotCalled(t, "Send", mock.Anything) // Send should not be called

    // Clean up timer
    if !sess.bkgTimer.Stop() {
       select { case <-sess.bkgTimer.C: default: }
    }

Test Implementation:
func TestServeGrpc_NoTLS_KA_793(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    addr := ":0" // Use ":0" to let the OS pick a free port
    kaEnabled := true
    tlsConf := (*tls.Config)(nil) // Explicitly nil TLS config

    // Mock netListener to return a dummy listener
    dummyListener := &net.TCPListener{} // A non-nil listener is enough for this part
    originalNetListener := netListener
    netListener = func(address string) (net.Listener, error) {
        // We need a real listener to allow Serve to be called without error,
        // but we close it immediately as we don't need the server running.
        lis, err := net.Listen("tcp", address)
        if err != nil {
             return nil, err // Propagate listen error
        }
        return lis, nil // Return the real listener
    }
    defer func() { netListener = originalNetListener }()

    // Act
    server, err := serveGrpc(addr, kaEnabled, tlsConf)

    // Assert
    require.NoError(t, err, "serveGrpc should not return error with valid config")

func TestServeGrpc_WithTLSAndKeepAlive_559(t *testing.T) {

    // Mock netListener to provide a real, temporary listener
    originalNetListener := netListener
    var lis net.Listener
    var lisErr error
    netListener = func(address string) (net.Listener, error) {

        if lisErr != nil {
             return nil, lisErr
        }
        return lis, nil
    }
    defer func() { netListener = originalNetListener }() // Restore original

    // Act

    // Assert
    require.NoError(t, err)
    require.NotNil(t, server)
    require.NoError(t, lisErr, "net.Listen should succeed") // Check listener creation
    require.NotNil(t, lis, "Listener should not be nil")

    // Clean up: Stop the server and close the listener
    if server != nil {
        server.Stop() // Stops the gRPC server gracefully
    }
     if lis != nil {
         lis.Close() // Close the network listener
     }

func TestPresParamsPackAcs_VariousScenarios_013(t *testing.T) {
    t.Run("Both dWant and dGiven are set", func(t *testing.T) {
        p := &presParams{dWant: "RW", dGiven: "P"}
        acs := p.packAcs()
        require.NotNil(t, acs)
        assert.Equal(t, "RW", acs.Want)
        assert.Equal(t, "P", acs.Given)
    })

    t.Run("Only dWant is set", func(t *testing.T) {
        p := &presParams{dWant: "R"}
        acs := p.packAcs()
        require.NotNil(t, acs)
        assert.Equal(t, "R", acs.Want)
        assert.Equal(t, "", acs.Given)
    })

    t.Run("Only dGiven is set", func(t *testing.T) {
        p := &presParams{dGiven: "W"}
        acs := p.packAcs()
        require.NotNil(t, acs)
        assert.Equal(t, "", acs.Want)
        assert.Equal(t, "W", acs.Given)
    })

    t.Run("Neither dWant nor dGiven is set", func(t *testing.T) {
        p := &presParams{}
        acs := p.packAcs()
        assert.Nil(t, acs)
    })
}

Test Implementation:
func TestTopicAddToPerSubs_VariousScenarios_222(t *testing.T) {
    t.Run("Skip adding self", func(t *testing.T) {
        topic := &Topic{name: "testTopic", perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        topic.addToPerSubs("testTopic", true, true)
        assert.Empty(t, topic.perSubs, "Should not add self to perSubs")
    })

    t.Run("Add non-P2P topic", func(t *testing.T) {
        topic := &Topic{name: "testTopic", perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        topic.addToPerSubs("anotherTopic", true, false)
        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, "anotherTopic")
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: true, enabled: false}, topic.perSubs["anotherTopic"])
    })

    t.Run("Add P2P topic where topic user is uid1", func(t *testing.T) {
        uid1 := types.ParseUserId("usr123")
        uid2 := types.ParseUserId("usr456")
        p2pTopicName := uid1.P2PName(uid2) // generates "usr123usr456" assuming Compare is correct

        topic := &Topic{name: uid1.UserId(), perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        topic.addToPerSubs(p2pTopicName, true, true)

        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, uid2.UserId(), "Should index P2P topic by the other user's ID")
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: true, enabled: true}, topic.perSubs[uid2.UserId()])
    })

    t.Run("Add P2P topic where topic user is uid2", func(t *testing.T) {
        uid1 := types.ParseUserId("usr123")
        uid2 := types.ParseUserId("usr456")
        p2pTopicName := uid1.P2PName(uid2) // generates "usr123usr456"

        topic := &Topic{name: uid2.UserId(), perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        topic.addToPerSubs(p2pTopicName, false, false)

        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, uid1.UserId(), "Should index P2P topic by the other user's ID")
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: false, enabled: false}, topic.perSubs[uid1.UserId()])
    })

    t.Run("Add P2P topic with invalid name (should treat as non-P2P)", func(t *testing.T) {
        topic := &Topic{name: "testTopic", perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        invalidP2PName := "invalidP2P" // This won't parse correctly with types.ParseP2P
        topic.addToPerSubs(invalidP2PName, true, true)
        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, invalidP2PName)
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: true, enabled: true}, topic.perSubs[invalidP2PName])
    })
}

Test Implementation:
func TestTopicLoadContacts_SuccessAndError_333(t *testing.T) {
    uid := types.ParseUserId("usr123")

    t.Run("Success case", func(t *testing.T) {
        mockCtrl := gomock.NewController(t)
        defer mockCtrl.Finish()
        mockStoreUsers := storeMocks.NewMockUsersPersistenceInterface(mockCtrl)

        // Save original and restore after test
        originalStoreUsers := store.Users
        store.Users = mockStoreUsers // Assign the mock
        defer func() { store.Users = originalStoreUsers }()

        subs := []types.Subscription{
            {
                ObjHeader: types.ObjHeader{Id: "sub1"},
                User:      uid.UserId(),
                Topic:     "topic1",
                ModeGiven: types.ModeRead | types.ModePres, // Presencer = true
                ModeWant:  types.ModeRead | types.ModePres,
            },
            {
                ObjHeader: types.ObjHeader{Id: "sub2"},
                User:      uid.UserId(),
                Topic:     "topic2",
                ModeGiven: types.ModeRead, // Presencer = false
                ModeWant:  types.ModeRead | types.ModePres,
            },
            {
                ObjHeader: types.ObjHeader{Id: "sub3"},
                User:      uid.UserId(),
                Topic:     types.ParseUserId("usr123").P2PName(types.ParseUserId("usr456")), // P2P topic
                ModeGiven: types.ModeJoin | types.ModePres,                                  // Presencer = true
                ModeWant:  types.ModeJoin | types.ModePres,
            },
            {
                ObjHeader: types.ObjHeader{Id: "sub4"},
                User:      uid.UserId(),
                Topic:     "usr123", // Should be skipped
                ModeGiven: types.ModeJoin | types.ModePres,
                ModeWant:  types.ModeJoin | types.ModePres,
            },
        }

        mockStoreUsers.EXPECT().GetSubs(uid).Return(subs, nil)

        topic := &Topic{name: uid.UserId(), perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        err := topic.loadContacts(uid)

        assert.NoError(t, err)
        require.Len(t, topic.perSubs, 3, "Expected 3 entries in perSubs")
        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, "topic1")
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: false, enabled: true}, topic.perSubs["topic1"])
        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, "topic2")
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: false, enabled: false}, topic.perSubs["topic2"])
        require.Contains(t, topic.perSubs, "usr456") // P2P topic indexed by other user
        assert.Equal(t, perSubsData{online: false, enabled: true}, topic.perSubs["usr456"])
        assert.NotContains(t, topic.perSubs, "usr123", "Should skip self topic") // Ensure self is not added
    })

    t.Run("Error case", func(t *testing.T) {
        mockCtrl := gomock.NewController(t)
        defer mockCtrl.Finish()
        mockStoreUsers := storeMocks.NewMockUsersPersistenceInterface(mockCtrl)

        // Save original and restore after test
        originalStoreUsers := store.Users
        store.Users = mockStoreUsers // Assign the mock
        defer func() { store.Users = originalStoreUsers }()

        expectedErr := errors.New("database error")
        mockStoreUsers.EXPECT().GetSubs(uid).Return(nil, expectedErr)

        topic := &Topic{name: uid.UserId(), perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData)}
        err := topic.loadContacts(uid)

        assert.Error(t, err)
        assert.Equal(t, expectedErr, err)
        assert.Empty(t, topic.perSubs, "perSubs should be empty on error")
    })
}

        },
        {

                 return topic
             }(),

            what:         "off+dis",
            wantReply:    false,
            expectedWhat: "",               // No update forwarded as user was already offline (line 170-172)
            expectedPerSub: map[string]perSubsData{"existingUser": {online: false, enabled: false}}, // Disabled
            expectReply:    false,
        },
        {

              topicState: func() *Topic {
