                 topic.perSubs["existingUser"] = perSubsData{online: false, enabled: false}
                 return topic
             }(),
            fromUserID:   "existingUser",
            what:         "off+en",
            wantReply:    true,
            expectedWhat: "", // No update forwarded as user offline->offline (line 163-166)
            expectedPerSub: map[string]perSubsData{"existingUser": {online: false, enabled: true}}, // Enabled
            expectReply:    false, // onlineUpdate=false (online=nil), reqReply=false
        },
        {
            name:           "unknown what",
            topicState:     newMeTopic("meUser"),
            fromUserID:     "someUser",
            what:           "invalid",
            wantReply:      false,
            expectedWhat:   "invalid", // Should return original invalid 'what'
            expectedPerSub: map[string]perSubsData{}, // No change
            expectReply:    false,
        },
        {
            name:           "off+rem from non-existent user (ignore)",
            topicState:     newMeTopic("meUser"),
            fromUserID:     "nonExistentUser",
            what:           "off+rem",
            wantReply:      true,
            expectedWhat:   "", // Ignored (line 200-202)
            expectedPerSub: map[string]perSubsData{}, // No change
            expectReply:    false, // No reply needed for ignored remove
        },
        {
            name: "non-me topic category (e.g. grp)",
            topicState: &Topic{
                name:    "grpTopic",
                cat:     types.TopicCatGrp, // Not 'me'
                perSubs: make(map[string]perSubsData),
                 subs:    make(map[string]*Subscription), // Ensure topic is active
            },
            fromUserID:     "someUser",
            what:           "on",
            wantReply:      true,
            expectedWhat:   "on", // Should return 'what' after basic processing
            expectedPerSub: map[string]perSubsData{}, // perSubs not modified for non-me
            expectReply:    true, // Reply sent because onlineUpdate=true and wantReply=true
            expectedReply:  &ServerComMessage{Pres: &MsgServerPres{Topic: "me", What: "on", Src: "grpTopic", WantReply: false}, RcptTo: "someUser"},
        },
    }

    for _, tt := range tests {
        t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
            // Clear the channel before each test
            for len(testHub.routeSrv) > 0 {
                <-testHub.routeSrv
            }

            // Make a deep copy of perSubs for assertion, as it's modified in place.
            expectedState := make(map[string]perSubsData)
            for k, v := range tt.expectedPerSub {
                expectedState[k] = v
            }

            resultWhat := tt.topicState.procPresReq(tt.fromUserID, tt.what, tt.wantReply)

            assert.Equal(t, tt.expectedWhat, resultWhat, "Mismatch in returned 'what'")
            assert.Equal(t, expectedState, tt.topicState.perSubs, "Mismatch in final perSubs state")

            if tt.expectReply {
                select {
                case reply := <-testHub.routeSrv:
                    require.NotNil(t, reply, "Expected non-nil reply")
                    require.NotNil(t, tt.expectedReply, "Expected non-nil expected reply")
                    assert.Equal(t, tt.expectedReply.RcptTo, reply.RcptTo, "Reply RcptTo mismatch")
                    require.NotNil(t, reply.Pres, "Expected non-nil Pres in reply")
                    require.NotNil(t, tt.expectedReply.Pres, "Expected non-nil Pres in expected reply")
                    assert.Equal(t, tt.expectedReply.Pres.Topic, reply.Pres.Topic, "Reply Pres.Topic mismatch")
                    assert.Equal(t, tt.expectedReply.Pres.Src, reply.Pres.Src, "Reply Pres.Src mismatch")
                    assert.Equal(t, tt.expectedReply.Pres.What, reply.Pres.What, "Reply Pres.What mismatch")
                    assert.Equal(t, tt.expectedReply.Pres.WantReply, reply.Pres.WantReply, "Reply Pres.WantReply mismatch")
                case <-time.After(100 * time.Millisecond): // Timeout to prevent hanging
                    t.Errorf("Expected a reply message, but none was sent")
                }
            } else {
                select {
                case unexpectedReply := <-testHub.routeSrv:
                    t.Errorf("Did not expect a reply message, but got one: %+v", unexpectedReply)
                default:
                    // Correct, no reply sent
                }
            }
        })
    }
}

func TestHistogramString_MarshalError_843(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange: Create a histogram that might cause marshaling issues (e.g., NaN, Inf)
    // Note: Standard JSON marshaller handles NaN/Inf, making it hard to force an error.
    // This test primarily checks the error handling path, even if the error
    // condition is unlikely with the current histogram struct definition.
    h := &histogram{
        Sum:    1.0 / 0.0, // Simulate potential issue, though json.Marshal handles Inf
        Bounds: []float64{1.0},
        CountPerBucket: []int64{0, 0},
    }

    // Act
    result := h.String()

    // Assert
    // Because json.Marshal handles Inf/NaN, it won't return an error here.
    // If it *did* fail, we'd expect "".
    // We assert the actual output which will be non-empty JSON.
    // A more robust test would mock json.Marshal to return an error.
    assert.NotEmpty(t, result) // In a real failure scenario, assert.Empty(t, result)
}

import (
	"expvar"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"runtime" // Import runtime for NumGoroutine check
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

Test Implementation:
func TestStatsInit_ValidPath_666(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    mux := http.NewServeMux()
    path := "/teststats_666" // Unique path
    originalStatsUpdate := globals.statsUpdate // Save original state
    globals.statsUpdate = nil                 // Ensure it's nil initially

     // Act
    statsInit(mux, path)

    // Ensure cleanup happens even on failure
    defer func() {
        // Need to shut down the goroutine started by statsInit
        if ch := globals.statsUpdate; ch != nil {
            // Drain any pending updates first to prevent deadlock
            go func() {
                for range ch {}
            }()
            // Send shutdown signal
            ch <- nil
            // Wait briefly for the goroutine to potentially exit
            time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond)
            // Set to nil as the updater does
            globals.statsUpdate = nil
        }
        // Restore original channel state
        globals.statsUpdate = originalStatsUpdate
        // Attempt to clean up expvars (best effort, expvar has no unpublish)
        // We rely on unique names or simply ignore potential remnants in other tests
         expvar.Get("Uptime") // Access to avoid "declared but not used" if not asserted below
         expvar.Get("NumGoroutines")

    }()


    // Assert
    require.NotNil(t, globals.statsUpdate, "globals.statsUpdate should be initialized")
    assert.Equal(t, 1024, cap(globals.statsUpdate), "globals.statsUpdate should have capacity 1024")

    // Check if the handler is registered by trying to serve a request
    req, err := http.NewRequest("GET", path, nil)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    recorder := httptest.NewRecorder()
    mux.ServeHTTP(recorder, req)
    // We expect expvar handler to return OK and some JSON content
    assert.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, recorder.Code)
    // Use specific var names registered by statsInit
    assert.Contains(t, recorder.Body.String(), `"Uptime"`)
    assert.Contains(t, recorder.Body.String(), `"NumGoroutines"`)

    // Check if default expvars are published
    uptimeVar := expvar.Get("Uptime")
    require.NotNil(t, uptimeVar)
    _, ok := uptimeVar.(expvar.Func) // Check type
    assert.True(t, ok)

    goroutineVar := expvar.Get("NumGoroutines")
    require.NotNil(t, goroutineVar)
    _, ok = goroutineVar.(expvar.Func) // Check type
    assert.True(t, ok)

    // Check values (Goroutines > 0, Uptime >= 0)
    assert.True(t, goroutineVar.(expvar.Func)().(int) > 0)
    // Allow for slight negative due to timing, check >= -0.1
    assert.True(t, uptimeVar.(expvar.Func)().(float64) >= -0.1)
}

func TestStatsRegisterHistogram_Success_144(t *testing.T) {

    name := "TestHistVarRegSuccess_144" // Unique name
    bounds := []float64{1.5, 2.5, 3.5}
    // Ensure var does not exist from previous runs (best effort check)
    expvar.Get(name)


    // Act
    statsRegisterHistogram(name, bounds)

    assert.Equal(t, bounds, hist.Bounds, "Bounds should match")
    expectedBucketCount := len(bounds) + 1
    require.Len(t, hist.CountPerBucket, expectedBucketCount, "Bucket count should be len(bounds)+1")
    // Check buckets are initialized to zero
    for _, count := range hist.CountPerBucket {
        assert.Equal(t, int64(0), count)
    }
    assert.Equal(t, int64(0), hist.Count)
    assert.Equal(t, 0.0, hist.Sum)
    expectedJSON := `{"count":0,"sum":0,"count_per_bucket":[0,0,0,0],"bounds":[1.5,2.5,3.5]}`
    assert.JSONEq(t, expectedJSON, hist.String())


    // Cleanup (optional, relies on unique names)
}

import (
	"expvar"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

Test Implementation:
func TestStatsUpdater_AllOperations_466(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    originalStatsUpdate := globals.statsUpdate
    globals.statsUpdate = make(chan *varUpdate, 10) // Buffered channel for updates
    defer func() {
        // Ensure channel is properly handled even if test fails before shutdown
        if ch := globals.statsUpdate; ch != nil && !isClosed(ch) {
            close(ch)
            // Drain potentially remaining items after failed test
            go func() { for range ch {} }()
        }
        globals.statsUpdate = originalStatsUpdate
     }()


    // Register variables for testing with unique names
    intVarName := "UpdaterIntVarTest_466"
    histVarName := "UpdaterHistVarTest_466"
    bounds := []float64{5.0, 15.0}
    // Ensure vars don't exist from previous runs (best effort check)
    expvar.Get(intVarName)
    expvar.Get(histVarName)

    statsRegisterInt(intVarName)
    statsRegisterHistogram(histVarName, bounds)

    // Start the updater in a goroutine
    updaterDone := make(chan bool)
    go func() {
        statsUpdater() // This will run until nil is received
        close(updaterDone)
    }()

    // Send updates via the channel directly
    globals.statsUpdate <- &varUpdate{varname: intVarName, value: int64(100), inc: false} // Set
    globals.statsUpdate <- &varUpdate{varname: intVarName, value: int64(50), inc: true}  // Inc
    globals.statsUpdate <- &varUpdate{varname: intVarName, value: int64(-25), inc: true} // Dec
    globals.statsUpdate <- &varUpdate{varname: histVarName, value: 3.0}                  // Hist sample
    globals.statsUpdate <- &varUpdate{varname: histVarName, value: 7.0}                  // Hist sample
    globals.statsUpdate <- &varUpdate{varname: histVarName, value: 20.0}                 // Hist sample

    // Send shutdown signal directly
    globals.statsUpdate <- nil // Triggers break in statsUpdater loop

    // Wait for updater to finish
    select {
    case <-updaterDone:
        // Updater finished cleanly
    case <-time.After(200 * time.Millisecond): // Increased timeout
        t.Fatal("statsUpdater did not shut down")
    }

    // Assert Int variable state
    intEv := expvar.Get(intVarName)
    require.NotNil(t, intEv)
    intVar, ok := intEv.(*expvar.Int)
    require.True(t, ok)
    assert.Equal(t, int64(125), intVar.Value(), "Int value mismatch (100 + 50 - 25)") // 100 + 50 - 25 = 125

    // Assert Histogram variable state
    histEv := expvar.Get(histVarName)
    require.NotNil(t, histEv)
    histVar, ok := histEv.(*histogram)
    require.True(t, ok)
    assert.Equal(t, int64(3), histVar.Count, "Histogram count mismatch")
    assert.InDelta(t, 3.0+7.0+20.0, histVar.Sum, 0.001, "Histogram sum mismatch") // Use InDelta for float comparison
    // Buckets: (-inf, 5.0), [5.0, 15.0), [15.0, +inf)
    // Samples: 3.0 (bucket 0), 7.0 (bucket 1), 20.0 (bucket 2)
    assert.Equal(t, []int64{1, 1, 1}, histVar.CountPerBucket, "Histogram buckets mismatch")

    // Assert channel is now nil (due to shutdown logic in statsUpdater)
    assert.Nil(t, globals.statsUpdate, "globals.statsUpdate should be nil after shutdown")

    // Cleanup expvars (optional, relies on unique names)
}

func TestSendMessageGrpc_QueueLimitExceeded_529(t *testing.T) {

    const testQueueLimit = 2

    mockStream := new(pbxMocks.Node_MessageLoopServer)
    // Create session with the test limit size channel
    sess := &Session{
        sid:        "test-queue-limit",
        proto:      GRPC,
        send:       make(chan interface{}, testQueueLimit), // Use the test limit
        stop:       make(chan interface{}, 1),
        detach:     make(chan string, 1),
        bkgTimer:   time.NewTimer(1 * time.Hour), // Use helper?
        lock:       sync.Mutex{},
        grpcnode:   mockStream,
    }

    // Fill the queue
    for i := 0; i < testQueueLimit; i++ {
        // Use non-blocking send to fill the buffer quickly
        select {
        case sess.send <- &pbx.ServerMsg{}:
        default:
            t.Fatalf("Failed to fill send queue buffer")
        }
    }
    // Ensure the queue is actually full
    require.Len(t, sess.send, testQueueLimit, "Send queue should be full")

    // Mock stats (optional, prevents nil pointer if statsInc is called)
    origStatsInc := statsInc
    statsInc = func(name string, value int64) {}
    defer func() { statsInc = origStatsInc }()

    // Act
    result := sess.sendMessageGrpc(&pbx.ServerMsg{Message: &pbx.ServerMsg_Ctrl{Ctrl: &pbx.ServerCtrl{Id: "overlimit"}}})

    // Assert
    assert.False(t, result, "sendMessageGrpc should return false when queue limit is exceeded")
    mockStream.AssertNotCalled(t, "Send", mock.Anything) // Send should not be called

    // Clean up timer
    sess.stopTimer()

func TestWriteGrpcLoop_BatchMsg_331(t *testing.T) {
	// Arrange
	mockStream := new(pbxMocks.Node_MessageLoopServer)
	sess := newTestSession(mockStream)
	sess.proto = GRPC // To test closeGrpc effect

	// Mock serializeAndUpdateStats
	serializedMsg1 := &pbx.ServerMsg{Message: &pbx.ServerMsg_Ctrl{Ctrl: &pbx.ServerCtrl{Id: "batch1", Code: 200}}}
	serializedMsg2 := &pbx.ServerMsg{Message: &pbx.ServerMsg_Ctrl{Ctrl: &pbx.ServerCtrl{Id: "batch2", Code: 200}}}
	sess.mockSerialize = func(msg *ServerComMessage) interface{} {
		if msg.Ctrl.Id == "batch1" {
			return serializedMsg1
		}
		if msg.Ctrl.Id == "batch2" {
			return serializedMsg2
		}
		return &pbx.ServerMsg{}
	}

	batch := []*ServerComMessage{
		{Ctrl: &MsgServerCtrl{Id: "batch1", Code: 200}},
		{Ctrl: &MsgServerCtrl{Id: "batch2", Code: 200}},
	}


	// Mock stream Send for both messages in the batch
	mockStream.On("Send", serializedMsg1).Return(nil).Once()
	mockStream.On("Send", serializedMsg2).Return(nil).Once()

	// Mock stats
	origStatsInc := statsInc
	statsInc = func(name string, value int64) {}
	defer func() { statsInc = origStatsInc }()

	// Start the loop in a goroutine
	loopExited := make(chan bool, 1)
	go func(){
    	sess.writeGrpcLoop()
    	loopExited <- true
    }()

	// Act: Send the batch to the channel
	sess.send <- batch
	time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond) // Allow time for processing

	// Stop the loop
	close(sess.stop)

	// Wait for loop to exit
	select {
    case <- loopExited:
         // Loop exited as expected
    case <- time.After(100 * time.Millisecond):
        t.Fatal("writeGrpcLoop did not exit after stop signal")
    }


	// Assert
	mockStream.AssertCalled(t, "Send", serializedMsg1)
	mockStream.AssertCalled(t, "Send", serializedMsg2)
	mockStream.AssertExpectations(t)

    sess.lock.Lock()
    node := sess.grpcnode
    sess.lock.Unlock()
    assert.Nil(t, node, "grpcnode should be nil after loop exits (deferred closeGrpc)")

    // Clean up timer (already stopped by loop exit)
}

    detachTopic := "grpTestTopic123"

    sess.subs[detachTopic] = &Subscription{} // Add a dummy subscription

    go func() {
        sess.writeGrpcLoop()
        loopExited <- true
    }()

    // Act
    sess.detach <- detachTopic
    time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond) // Allow time for processing detach

    close(sess.stop)
    select {
        case <- loopExited:
        case <- time.After(100 * time.Millisecond): t.Fatal("writeGrpcLoop did not exit")
    }

    mockStream.AssertNotCalled(t, "Send", mock.Anything) // Detach shouldn't send messages

    // sess.stopTimer() // Timer stopped by loop exit
}

    }

	// Act

	err := grpcServer.MessageLoop(mockStream)

	// Assert

	mockSessStore.AssertCalled(t, "NewSession", mockStream, "")
	mockStream.AssertCalled(t, "Context")

func TestWriteOnce_SendSerializedMessage_890(t *testing.T) {
  // Arrange
  sess := makeTestSession("sid123")
  wrt := httptest.NewRecorder()
  req := httptest.NewRequest("GET", "/lp?sid=sid123", nil)
  testMsg := []byte(`{"ctrl":{"id":"1","code":200,"text":"OK"}}`)

  go func() {
    sess.send <- testMsg
  }()

  // Act
  sess.writeOnce(wrt, req)

  // Assert
  assert.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, wrt.Code) // Default status
  assert.Equal(t, string(testMsg), wrt.Body.String())

  // Clean up channels

func TestWriteOnce_BackgroundTimerFires_BackgroundTrue_654(t *testing.T) {
  // Arrange
  sess := makeTestSession("sid123")
  sess.background = true
  // Use a timer that fires immediately
  sess.bkgTimer = time.NewTimer(1 * time.Millisecond)
  // Mock onBackgroundTimer if needed, or just check sess.background
  originalOnBackgroundTimer := sess.onBackgroundTimer // Assuming onBackgroundTimer exists
  backgroundTimerCalled := false
  sess.onBackgroundTimer = func() {
      backgroundTimerCalled = true
  }
  defer func() { sess.onBackgroundTimer = originalOnBackgroundTimer }()


  wrt := httptest.NewRecorder()
  req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(context.Background(), "GET", "/lp?sid=sid123", nil)

  // Act
  // Use a timeout since writeOnce might loop after handling the timer
  ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 100*time.Millisecond)
  defer cancel()

  done := make(chan bool)
  go func() {
      // Need to cancel the request context eventually to make writeOnce exit the loop
      time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)
      cancel() // This will trigger <-req.Context().Done() case
      done <- true
  }()

  sess.writeOnce(wrt, req.WithContext(ctx)) // Pass the cancellable context

  <-done // Wait for the goroutine to finish

  // Assert
  assert.False(t, sess.background, "sess.background should be false after timer")
  assert.True(t, backgroundTimerCalled, "onBackgroundTimer should have been called")
  // We expect the body to be empty because we canceled before any other message could be sent.

  // Clean up channels
  close(sess.send)
  close(sess.stop)
  close(sess.detach)
  // sess.bkgTimer is already handled
}

  defer restoreGlobals()

  mockStore := newMockSessionStore()
  globals.sessionStore = mockStore // Assign mock store to globals
  defer func() { globals.sessionStore = nil }() // Cleanup

  newSid := "newSid123"
  newSess := makeTestSession(newSid)
  expectedCount := 5

  // Mock NewSession
  mockStore.On("NewSession", mock.Anything, "").Return(newSess, expectedCount)

  wrt := httptest.NewRecorder()
  req := httptest.NewRequest("POST", "/lp?apikey=test-api-key&id=req1", nil) // No sid, valid apikey

  assert.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, wrt.Code)
  assert.Equal(t, "text/plain", wrt.Header().Get("Content-Type"))
  assert.Equal(t, "max-age31536000", wrt.Header().Get("Strict-Transport-Security"))
  assert.Equal(t, "*", wrt.Header().Get("Access-Control-Allow-Origin"))
  assert.Equal(t, "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate", wrt.Header().Get("Cache-Control"))
  assert.Equal(t, "0", wrt.Header().Get("Expires"))

  assert.NoError(t, err)
  assert.NotNil(t, respMsg.Ctrl)
  assert.Equal(t, "req1", respMsg.Ctrl.Id)
  assert.Equal(t, http.StatusCreated, int(respMsg.Ctrl.Code))
  assert.Equal(t, "Created", respMsg.Ctrl.Text)
  assert.Equal(t, newSid, respMsg.Ctrl.Params.(map[string]interface{})["sid"])
  assert.Equal(t, req.RemoteAddr, newSess.remoteAddr) // Check remoteAddr was set


  // Clean up channels for the created session
  close(newSess.send)
  close(newSess.stop)
  close(newSess.detach)
  newSess.bkgTimer.Stop()
}

func TestServeLongPoll_ExistingSession_RemoteAddrChange_125(t *testing.T) {
  // Arrange
  restoreGlobals := setupTestGlobals(1024, false, "test-api-key", "")
  defer restoreGlobals()

  mockStore := newMockSessionStore()
  globals.sessionStore = mockStore // Assign mock store to globals
  defer func() { globals.sessionStore = nil }() // Cleanup

  existingSid := "existingSid789"
  sess := makeTestSession(existingSid)
  originalAddr := "10.0.0.1:54321"
  newAddr := "10.0.0.2:12345"
  sess.remoteAddr = originalAddr

  mockStore.On("Get", existingSid).Return(sess)
  mockStore.SetSession(sess)

  wrt := httptest.NewRecorder()
  req := httptest.NewRequest("GET", "/lp?apikey=test-api-key&sid="+existingSid, nil)
  req.RemoteAddr = newAddr // New remote addr

  // Make writeOnce return quickly (e.g., context cancel)
  ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
  req = req.WithContext(ctx)
  go func() {
      time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond)
      cancel()
  }()

  // Act
  serveLongPoll(wrt, req)

  // Assert
  mockStore.AssertCalled(t, "Get", existingSid)
  assert.Equal(t, newAddr, sess.remoteAddr, "Session remote address should be updated")
  // Check logs if possible for the warning message

  // Clean up channels
  close(sess.send)
  close(sess.stop)
  close(sess.detach)
  sess.bkgTimer.Stop()
}

func TestServeLongPoll_ExistingSession_WithPayload_ReadSuccess_881(t *testing.T) {
  // Arrange
  restoreGlobals := setupTestGlobals(1024, false, "test-api-key", "")
  defer restoreGlobals()

  mockStore := newMockSessionStore()
  globals.sessionStore = mockStore // Assign mock store to globals
  defer func() { globals.sessionStore = nil }() // Cleanup

  existingSid := "existingSid789"
  sess := makeTestSession(existingSid)
  sess.remoteAddr = "10.0.0.1:54321"

  mockStore.On("Get", existingSid).Return(sess)
  mockStore.SetSession(sess)

  // Mock dispatchRaw
  var dispatchedData []byte
  originalDispatchRaw := sess.dispatchRaw
  sess.dispatchRaw = func(raw []byte) {
      dispatchedData = raw
  }
  defer func() { sess.dispatchRaw = originalDispatchRaw }()


  wrt := httptest.NewRecorder()
  reqBodyContent := `{"pub":{"id":"pub1","topic":"grpABC","content":"hello"}}`
  reqBody := bytes.NewReader([]byte(reqBodyContent))
  req := httptest.NewRequest("POST", "/lp?apikey=test-api-key&sid="+existingSid, reqBody)
  req.RemoteAddr = "10.0.0.1:54321"
  req.ContentLength = int64(len(reqBodyContent))

  // Act
  serveLongPoll(wrt, req)

  // Assert
  mockStore.AssertCalled(t, "Get", existingSid)
  assert.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, wrt.Code) // Should be OK if readOnce succeeds
  assert.Empty(t, wrt.Body.String(), "No body should be written immediately after successful read")
  assert.Equal(t, reqBodyContent, string(dispatchedData), "dispatchRaw should receive the payload")

  // Clean up channels
  close(sess.send)
  close(sess.stop)
  close(sess.detach)
  sess.bkgTimer.Stop()
}

func TestServeLongPoll_ExistingSession_WithPayload_ReadFailsCode_773(t *testing.T) {
  // Arrange
  restoreGlobals := setupTestGlobals(50, false, "test-api-key", "") // Small max size
  defer restoreGlobals()

  mockStore := newMockSessionStore()
  globals.sessionStore = mockStore // Assign mock store to globals
  defer func() { globals.sessionStore = nil }() // Cleanup

  existingSid := "existingSid789"
  sess := makeTestSession(existingSid)
  sess.remoteAddr = "10.0.0.1:54321"

  mockStore.On("Get", existingSid).Return(sess)
  mockStore.SetSession(sess)

  wrt := httptest.NewRecorder()
  reqBodyContent := `{"pub":{"id":"pub1","topic":"grpABC","content":"this message is definitely larger than fifty bytes"}}`
  reqBody := bytes.NewReader([]byte(reqBodyContent))
  req := httptest.NewRequest("POST", "/lp?apikey=test-api-key&sid="+existingSid+"&id=reqFail", reqBody)
  req.RemoteAddr = "10.0.0.1:54321"
  req.ContentLength = int64(len(reqBodyContent)) // Exceeds maxMessageSize

  // Act
  serveLongPoll(wrt, req)

  // Assert
  mockStore.AssertCalled(t, "Get", existingSid)
  // ExpectationFailed comes from readOnce
  assert.Equal(t, http.StatusExpectationFailed, wrt.Code)
  // The error response comes from serveLongPoll
  var respMsg ServerComMessage
  err := json.Unmarshal(wrt.Body.Bytes(), &respMsg)
  assert.NoError(t, err)
  assert.NotNil(t, respMsg.Ctrl)
  assert.Equal(t, "reqFail", respMsg.Ctrl.Id)
  assert.Equal(t, http.StatusBadRequest, int(respMsg.Ctrl.Code)) // ErrMalformed code
  assert.Equal(t, "Malformed request", respMsg.Ctrl.Text)

  // Clean up channels
  close(sess.send)
  close(sess.stop)
  close(sess.detach)
  sess.bkgTimer.Stop()
}

func TestWriteOnce_SendMessageLpFails_Serialized_357(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    sess := makeTestSession("sid123")
    wrt := &mockResponseWriter{ResponseWriter: httptest.NewRecorder()} // Use mock writer
    wrt.err = errors.New("write failed")                               // Simulate write error
    req := httptest.NewRequest("GET", "/lp?sid=sid123", nil)
    testMsg := []byte(`{"data":{"topic":"usrABC","content":"hi"}}`)

    go func() {
      sess.send <- testMsg
    }()

    // Act
    sess.writeOnce(wrt, req)

    // Assert
    assert.True(t, wrt.writeCalled > 0, "Write should have been attempted")
    assert.True(t, len(wrt.lastWrite) > 0, "Attempted write should not be empty")
    assert.Equal(t, string(testMsg), string(wrt.lastWrite))
    // No specific status code or body expected

    // Clean up channels
    // sess.send handled
    close(sess.stop)
    close(sess.detach)
    sess.bkgTimer.Stop()
}

Test Implementation:
func TestNormalizeTags_Mixed_459(t *testing.T) {
    minTagLength = 3
    maxTagLength = 10
    globals.maxTagCount = 5
    input := []string{" Long ", "ok", "duplicate", "_badstart", "duplicate", "  GOOD  ", "t", "toolongtagisbad", "ok"}
    // Expected: " Long " -> "long" (ok)
    // "ok" -> too short
    // "duplicate" -> "duplicate" (ok)
    // "_badstart" -> invalid start
    // "duplicate" -> removed
    // "  GOOD  " -> "good" (ok)
    // "t" -> too short
    // "toolongtagisbad" -> too long
    // "ok" -> too short
    // Result after limit (5): [" Long ", "ok", "duplicate", "_badstart", "duplicate"]
    // Result after normalization: ["duplicate", "long"]
    // Wait, limit applies *before* normalization.
    // So input becomes [" Long ", "ok", "duplicate", "_badstart", "duplicate"]
    // Then normalize: "long", "duplicate" -> sort -> ["duplicate", "long"]
    expected := types.StringSlice{"duplicate", "long"}
    result := normalizeTags(input)
    assert.Equal(t, expected, result, "Should handle mixed valid/invalid tags correctly")
    minTagLength = 2 // Reset
    maxTagLength = 96 // Reset
}

import (
	"sort"
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

Test Implementation:
func TestNormalizeCredentials_NoValueRequired_128(t *testing.T) {
    globals.validators = map[string]*validatorConfig{
        "email": {name: "email"},
        "tel":   {name: "tel"},
    }
    input := []MsgCredClient{
        {Method: "email", Value: "a@b.c"},
        {Method: "tel", Value: ""}, // Empty value allowed
        {Method: "email", Value: "d@e.f"}, // Duplicate method, last one wins
        {Method: "unknown", Value: "stuff"},
    }
    // Order is not guaranteed due to map iteration
    expected := []MsgCredClient{
         {Method: "tel", Value: ""},
         {Method: "email", Value: "d@e.f"},
    }
    result := normalizeCredentials(input, false)

    // Sort results for stable comparison
    sort.Slice(result, func(i, j int) bool {
         return result[i].Method < result[j].Method
    })
     sort.Slice(expected, func(i, j int) bool {
         return expected[i].Method < expected[j].Method
    })

    assert.ElementsMatch(t, expected, result, "Should keep valid methods, including empty values")
}

func TestRewriteTag_ValidatorMatch_132(t *testing.T) {
    mockValidatorInstance := new(mockValidator)
    mockStoreInstance := new(mockPersistentStorage)
    mockStoreInstance.validators = map[string]validate.Validator{
        "email": mockValidatorInstance,
    }
    globals.validators = map[string]*validatorConfig{
        "email": {name: "email", addToTags: true},
        "tel":   {name: "tel", addToTags: false}, // Should be ignored
    }

    origTag := "test@example.com"
    expectedTag := "email:test@example.com"
    countryCode := "US"
    params := map[string]any{"countryCode": countryCode}

    mockStoreInstance.On("GetValidator", "email").Return(mockValidatorInstance)
    mockValidatorInstance.On("PreCheck", origTag, params).Return(expectedTag, nil)

    // Mock other validators if GetValidator is called for them
    mockStoreInstance.On("GetValidator", "tel").Return(nil) // Assume tel validator not found or not mocked

    originalStore := store.Store
    store.Store = mockStoreInstance
    defer func() { store.Store = originalStore }()

    result := rewriteTag(origTag, countryCode, false) // withLogin = false

    assert.Equal(t, expectedTag, result, "Should return tag prefixed by validator")
    mockStoreInstance.AssertExpectations(t)
    mockValidatorInstance.AssertExpectations(t)
}

func TestWriteGrpcLoop_BatchMsg_111(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    mockStream := new(pbxMocks.Node_MessageLoopServer)
    sess := newTestSession(mockStream)
    sess.proto = GRPC // To test closeGrpc effect

    serializedMsg1 := &pbx.ServerMsg{Message: &pbx.ServerMsg_Ctrl{Ctrl: &pbx.ServerCtrl{Id: "batch1", Code: 200}}}
    serializedMsg2 := &pbx.ServerMsg{Message: &pbx.ServerMsg_Ctrl{Ctrl: &pbx.ServerCtrl{Id: "batch2", Code: 200}}}

    // Mock serializeAndUpdateStats
    origSerialize := sess.serializeAndUpdateStats
    sess.serializeAndUpdateStats = func(msg *ServerComMessage) interface{} {
        statsInc("test", 1) // Simulate stats call
        if msg.Ctrl.Id == "batch1" {
            return serializedMsg1
        }
        if msg.Ctrl.Id == "batch2" {
            return serializedMsg2
        }
        return &pbx.ServerMsg{}
    }
    defer func() { sess.serializeAndUpdateStats = origSerialize }()

    batch := []*ServerComMessage{
        {Ctrl: &MsgServerCtrl{Id: "batch1", Code: 200}},
        {Ctrl: &MsgServerCtrl{Id: "batch2", Code: 200}},
    }

    // Mock stream Send for both messages in the batch
    mockStream.On("Send", serializedMsg1).Return(nil).Once()
    mockStream.On("Send", serializedMsg2).Return(nil).Once()

    // Mock statsInc
    statsCalled := 0
    origStatsInc := statsInc
    statsInc = func(name string, value int64) { statsCalled++ }
    defer func() { statsInc = origStatsInc }()

    // Start the loop in a goroutine
    loopExited := make(chan bool, 1)
    go func() {
        sess.writeGrpcLoop()
        loopExited <- true
    }()

    // Act: Send the batch to the channel
    sess.send <- batch
    time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond) // Allow time for processing

    // Stop the loop
    close(sess.stop) // Closing stop channel triggers exit

    // Wait for loop to exit
    select {
    case <-loopExited:
        // Loop exited as expected
    case <-time.After(200 * time.Millisecond): // Increased timeout
        t.Fatal("writeGrpcLoop did not exit after stop signal")
    }

    // Assert
    mockStream.AssertCalled(t, "Send", serializedMsg1)
    mockStream.AssertCalled(t, "Send", serializedMsg2)
    mockStream.AssertExpectations(t)
    // Expect 2 calls from serializeAndUpdateStats + 2 calls from sendMessageGrpc
    assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, statsCalled, 4, "statsInc should be called for serialization and sending")

    sess.lock.Lock()
    node := sess.grpcnode
    sess.lock.Unlock()
    assert.Nil(t, node, "grpcnode should be nil after loop exits (deferred closeGrpc)")
}

    sess.bkgTimer.Reset(10 * time.Millisecond) // Use a short timer for testing

    // Mock onBackgroundTimer by checking its side effect

    sess.onBackgroundTimer = func() {
         sess.lock.Lock()
         sess.background = false // Simulate the original function's effect
         onBkgTimerCalled = true
         sess.lock.Unlock()
    }

    go func() {
        sess.writeGrpcLoop()
        loopExited <- true

    // Stop the loop

    case <-loopExited:
    case <-time.After(100 * time.Millisecond):
        t.Fatal("writeGrpcLoop did not exit")

    // Assert
    assert.True(t, onBkgTimerCalled, "onBackgroundTimer should have been called")
    sess.lock.Lock()
    bgFlag := sess.background
    sess.lock.Unlock()
    assert.False(t, bgFlag, "Session background flag should be false after timer tick")

    sess.stop <- nil // Send nil to stop channel

    // Wait for loop to exit
    select {
    case <-loopExited:
        // Loop exited as expected
    case <-time.After(100 * time.Millisecond):
        t.Fatal("writeGrpcLoop did not exit after nil stop signal")
    }

    // Assert
    mockStream.AssertNotCalled(t, "Send", mock.Anything) // No final message sent

    // Check if closeGrpc was called (it should be called by defer)
    sess.lock.Lock()
    node := sess.grpcnode
    sess.lock.Unlock()
    // NOTE: The defer sess.closeGrpc() WILL run when the loop exits.
    assert.Nil(t, node, "grpcnode should be nil after deferred closeGrpc runs")

    detachTopic := "grpTestTopic123"

    var deletedTopic string
    sess.delSub = func(topic string) {
        delSubCalled = true
        deletedTopic = topic
    }

    loopExited := make(chan bool, 1)
    go func() {
        sess.writeGrpcLoop()
        loopExited <- true
    }()
    time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond) // Let loop start

    // Act

    time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond) // Allow time for processing detach

    assert.Equal(t, detachTopic, deletedTopic, "delSub called with wrong topic")

    close(sess.stop) // Closing stop channel triggers exit
    select {
    case <-loopExited:
    case <-time.After(100 * time.Millisecond):
        t.Fatal("writeGrpcLoop did not exit")
    }

    mockStream.AssertNotCalled(t, "Send", mock.Anything) // Detach shouldn't send messages

         sess.grpcnode = nil
         sess.lock.Unlock()

    defer func() { statsInc = origStatsInc }()

    // Act
    grpcServer := &grpcNodeServer{}

    mockSessStore.On("NewSession", mockStream, "").Return(sess, 1).Once()

    sessCleanedUp := false
    sess.cleanUp = func(sync bool) { sessCleanedUp = true }
    // closeGrpc will be called by the defer, but also simulate node becoming nil earlier
    origCloseGrpc := sess.closeGrpc
    sess.closeGrpc = func() {
         origCloseGrpc() // Call original to ensure nil assignment
    }


    p := &peer.Peer{Addr: &net.TCPAddr{IP: net.ParseIP("127.0.0.1"), Port: 12345}}
    ctx := peer.NewContext(context.Background(), p)

    deserializedMsg1 := &ClientComMessage{Hi: &MsgClientHi{Id: "1"}}
    mockStream.On("Recv").Return(clientMsg1, nil).Run(func(args mock.Arguments) {
        // Simulate node becoming nil *after* dispatch but before next Recv check
        // This happens in the check `if sess.grpcnode == nil`
        go func() { // Use goroutine to avoid deadlock if dispatch blocks
             time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond) // Short delay
             sess.lock.Lock()
             sess.grpcnode = nil
             sess.lock.Unlock()
        }()
    }).Once()

    origDeserialize := pbCliDeserialize
    pbCliDeserialize = func(in *pbx.ClientMsg) *ClientComMessage { return deserializedMsg1 }

func TestMessageLoop_NoPeerInfo_010(t *testing.T) {
    // Arrange
    mockStream := new(pbxMocks.Node_MessageLoopServer)
    mockSessStore := new(mockSessionStore)

    savedStore := globals.sessionStore
    globals.sessionStore = mockSessStore
    defer func() { globals.sessionStore = savedStore }()

    sess := newTestSession(mockStream)
    sess.proto = GRPC
    mockSessStore.On("NewSession", mockStream, "").Return(sess, 1).Once()

    sessCleanedUp := false
    sess.cleanUp = func(sync bool) { sessCleanedUp = true }
    sess.closeGrpc = func() {
         sess.lock.Lock(); sess.grpcnode = nil; sess.lock.Unlock()
    }

    // Mock Context without peer info
    ctx := context.Background() // No peer attached
    mockStream.On("Context").Return(ctx).Once()

    // Mock Recv to return EOF immediately to exit loop cleanly
    mockStream.On("Recv").Return(nil, io.EOF).Once()

    // Mock Send just in case write loop starts
    mockStream.On("Send", mock.AnythingOfType("*pbx.ServerMsg")).Return(nil).Maybe()

    origStatsInc := statsInc
    statsInc = func(string, int64){}
    defer func() { statsInc = origStatsInc }()

    // Act
    grpcServer := &grpcNodeServer{}
    err := grpcServer.MessageLoop(mockStream)

    // Assert
    require.NoError(t, err, "MessageLoop should return nil on EOF even without peer info")
    assert.Empty(t, sess.remoteAddr, "remoteAddr should be empty when peer info is missing")
    mockSessStore.AssertCalled(t, "NewSession", mockStream, "")
    mockStream.AssertCalled(t, "Context")
    mockStream.AssertNumberOfCalls(t, "Recv", 1)
    assert.True(t, sessCleanedUp, "sess.cleanUp should be called")
    assert.Nil(t, sess.grpcnode, "sess.grpcnode should be nil after cleanup")

    mockStream.AssertExpectations(t)
    mockSessStore.AssertExpectations(t)
}

func TestNormalizeCredentials_NoValueRequired_014(t *testing.T) {
    // Setup globals.validators for this test. Using interface{} as placeholder for credValidator.
    // The function only checks for key existence.
    originalValidators := globals.validators
    globals.validators = map[string]credValidator{
        "email": nil, // Represents a valid method
        "tel":   nil, // Represents a valid method
    }
    defer func() { globals.validators = originalValidators }() // Restore original validators

    input := []MsgCredClient{
        {Method: "email", Value: "a@b.c"},
        {Method: "tel", Value: ""},         // Empty value allowed
        {Method: "email", Value: "d@e.f"},  // Duplicate method, this one should overwrite the first 'email'
        {Method: "unknown", Value: "stuff"},// Unknown method, should be filtered out
    }
    // Order is not guaranteed due to map iteration in the function.
    // Keep the last occurrence for duplicates.
    expected := []MsgCredClient{
         {Method: "tel", Value: ""},
         {Method: "email", Value: "d@e.f"},
    }
    result := normalizeCredentials(input, false)

    assert.ElementsMatch(t, expected, result, "Should keep valid methods, including empty values, handling duplicates")
}

--------------------Test Case--------------------
Import Statements:
import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

Test Implementation:
func TestNormalizeCredentials_ValueRequired_015(t *testing.T) {
    originalValidators := globals.validators
    globals.validators = map[string]credValidator{
        "email": nil,
        "tel":   nil,
    }
    defer func() { globals.validators = originalValidators }()

    input := []MsgCredClient{
        {Method: "email", Value: "a@b.c"},
        {Method: "tel", Value: ""},         // Empty value filtered out
        {Method: "email", Value: ""},         // Empty value filtered out (even if duplicate)
        {Method: "unknown", Value: "stuff"},// Unknown method filtered out
    }
    // Only email:a@b.c should remain. The second email overwrites the first, but its value is empty, so it's removed too.
    // Wait, the logic keeps the *last* valid one. So the second email replaces the first in the map `index`.
    // Then, when iterating the map `index`, it appends.
    // Let's trace:
    // 1. index["email"] = {Method: "email", Value: "a@b.c"}
    // 2. index["tel"] = {Method: "tel", Value: ""} -> removed because Value is empty when valueRequired=true
    // 3. index["email"] = {Method: "email", Value: ""} -> removed because Value is empty when valueRequired=true
    // 4. "unknown" skipped
    // Result should be empty. Let's re-read the code.
    // Line 172: `if _, ok := globals.validators[c.Method]; ok && (!valueRequired || c.Value != "")`
    // If valueRequired is true, it becomes `ok && (false || c.Value != "")` -> `ok && c.Value != ""`
    // Trace again with valueRequired=true:
    // 1. creds[0]: email, a@b.c -> ok=true, Value!="" -> index["email"] = &creds[0]
    // 2. creds[1]: tel, "" -> ok=true, Value=="" -> skip
    // 3. creds[2]: email, "" -> ok=true, Value=="" -> skip. index["email"] remains &creds[0]
    // 4. creds[3]: unknown -> ok=false -> skip
    // Final map `index`: {"email": &creds[0]}
    // Output loop iterates `index`: appends *index["email"] -> {Method: "email", Value: "a@b.c"}
    expected := []MsgCredClient{
        {Method: "email", Value: "a@b.c"},
    }
    result := normalizeCredentials(input, true)
    assert.ElementsMatch(t, expected, result, "Should keep only valid methods with non-empty values")
}
